frames_add.concerns: A full chapter of premarital sex with nudity (ch. 125); an on-page suicide honored as sacrifice (ch. 82-83); cannibalism as a source of strength (ch. 157, 163); sins borne by human will with no grace beyond it.

frames_add.aligns: 'The world merely exists,' yet Kaneki chooses to live and build coexistence, Furuta's nihilism is rejected, and research cures the ROS crisis (ch. 176-179).
frames_add.concerns: An honored on-page suicide and sexualized violence around a trans character (ch. 4, 73, 114).

frames_add.aligns: Christian imagery of sin and Christmas is used symbolically and never settled, and Ishida leaves unexplored parts for readers to imagine.
frames_add.concerns: Mass-casualty horror and explicit content well beyond most teens.

frames_add.aligns: Loyal friendship (Hide), a wife who never gives up on her husband, forgiveness and a hopeful family ending.
frames_add.concerns: Rated 16+: constant gore, an explicit sex chapter (ch. 125), suicide and abuse.

frames_add.aligns: Concern for a hunted minority and a plea for empathy across a hated divide; cycles of revenge condemned; friendship and sacrifice (Anteiku, Hide).
frames_add.concerns: Cannibalism, torture and graphic violence; strong language; a bleak ending with no saving answer beyond human striving.

frames_add.aligns: Humanity defined by empathy, not species; refusal of easy good and evil; religious imagery stays symbolic.
frames_add.concerns: Fighting made glamorous; mental-health crisis without support or recovery; bleak ending.

frames_add.aligns: Asks what makes someone human and leaves it open; both sides shown with fairness.
frames_add.concerns: Extreme content; despair heavy in the ending.

frames_add.aligns: Loyalty to friends (Hide) and a found family at Anteiku; prejudice shown as wrong.
frames_add.concerns: Despair and loss dominate the ending; cannibalism and torture are far beyond a child's age (parent guides say 15+).

frames_add.aligns: No one is beyond saving (Luke 15:4), revenge is shown to feed a cycle that kills (Romans 12:19), every violent path ends in death or prison, and former enemies end up serving orphans (ch. 278).
frames_add.concerns: Gang life is drawn with a style that can glamorize street violence, a suicide is framed as loyalty (ch. 61), an off-page sexual assault is used as backstory (ch. 12-14), and language is rough.

frames_add.aligns: Humans repair their own world by persistence and loyalty, with no supernatural judge, and manipulation (Kisaki) is exposed.

frames_add.aligns: Lust, envy and murder always end in ruin (James 1:14-15); nothing evil is called good.

frames_add.aligns: A few people survive because they are kind and not vain (Fumihito in 'Basement', Tsukiko in 'Kiss').
frames_add.concerns: Despair and an evil that always returns; cruelty everywhere; sexual content involving minors.

frames_add.aligns: Loyal friendship, honest apology, a romance that waits for a father's blessing (vol. 8), and a friend who stops a groper and reports him to police.

frames_add.aligns: Honest talk and friendship resolve years of misunderstanding, and Tomo is accepted as she is without anyone appealing to a higher authority.

frames_add.aligns: A gentle comedy that pushes no worldview and lets friends with different ideas about what a girl should be learn from each other.
frames_add.concerns: Fan service, comic violence between friends, and the handling of the bus assault's aftermath.

frames_add.aligns: Everyday loyalty, families who know and care for each other, and a happy ending where nobody has to become someone else.
frames_add.concerns: Fan service, friends hitting each other as a joke, and Jun telling Tomo to stop wearing skirts after she is groped.

frames_add.aligns: Friends over money (1 Timothy 6:10), a hero who takes torture for a friend (ch. 23-25), and a closing reckoning with past sin.

frames_add.aligns: Reason and cunning against a system that prices people, and accountability for the hero's crimes at the end.

frames_add.aligns: No religious claims; trust and forgiveness are argued out among people.

frames_add.aligns: Corrupt police who pin crimes on scapegoats are exposed (ch. 80-147), and a man treated as worthless by his mother finds loyal friends (ch. 70-72).

frames_add.aligns: Observation, probability and reason win rather than luck or providence, and powerful liars are exposed.

frames_add.aligns: No doctrine is pressed, and villains with rival philosophies are given real arguments before they lose.
frames_add.concerns: A world with no judge but an enforcement club that cares only for the wager; torture games and the child-exploitation backstory (ch. 236).

frames_add.aligns: Loyalty to a few trusted companions carries the story, and corrupt elites get payback (ch. 175-269).
frames_add.concerns: Glorified cruelty and executions under the terms of bets, gambling as a way of life, and the child-exploitation backstory (ch. 236).

frames_add.aligns: Nothing evil is made attractive, and loyal love between Kirie and Shuichi and between Kirie and her family lasts to the end (ch. 13-19).

frames_add.aligns: No faith or prayer is offered as the answer; Shuichi questions and investigates and is proved right, and the horror is plainly fiction.

frames_add.aligns: The spiral is left a mystery; even Ito says he is unsure what it means, and the book raises the question of human limits without answering it.

frames_add.aligns: The unfinished story asks what strength and life are for without forcing a final answer, and readers from many traditions find their own echoes in it.

frames_add.aligns: Finding your own path, a personal spiritual sense without church membership, forgiveness of a weak friend (Matahachi) and belonging to the land and a village fit this tradition closely.

frames_add.aligns: Slavery is indicted from the side of the enslaved (ch. 87-93), Vinland is a promised land without slavery, and a former killer turns to repentance and nonviolent love of enemies (ch. 96), close to Exodus, Matthew 5:44 and the nonviolence of the Civil Rights movement.

frames_add.aligns: Religious and secular readers can both read Thorfinn's change in their own way, and Willibald's questions about love and Canute's quarrel with God are left as real questions (ch. 39).

frames_add.aligns: Family, hard work, second chances and choosing to have no enemies are the heart of the story, and the hero comes home to his family at the end (vols. 28-29).

frames_add.aligns: Education and self-improvement as a path out of poverty, honoring a widowed mother (Ephesians 6:1-3), and helping others reach their goals.

frames_add.aligns: Effort, study and reason are rewarded, and the romantic fireworks legend is revealed as a story a man made up (ch. 187).

frames_add.aligns: Goodness comes from character and care rather than any command, and Iruma grows by his own effort and cleverness (Harvest Festival, ch. 102-140); the demons are plainly fantasy.

20th-century-boys.Historically Black Protestant: 1 John 4:1 says to test the spirits: how could the crowd have seen through Friend's staged miracles? Kenji answers his enemy with an apology; compare Romans 12:19-21.
20th-century-boys.Atheist: Friend's levitation is a trick: what questions would expose a fake miracle? Why do educated people still join groups like the Friends?
20th-century-boys.Agnostic: The story distrusts every messiah, even Kenji; is it fair to the sincere believers shown, like Father Nitani?
20th-century-boys.Nothing in particular: Kenji had one thing he could not run from; what is yours? Why did so many people follow someone whose face they never saw?

21st-century-boys.Historically Black Protestant: Talk about confession (1 John 1:9) and about forgiveness that is asked for but not given; also how a whole class failed one child.
21st-century-boys.Atheist: Ask why people wanted a messiah, how a man became one, and how false memories form.
21st-century-boys.Agnostic: Does Kenji's apology matter if the grown Katsumata refuses it? Can you make amends to someone in the past?
21st-century-boys.Nothing in particular: Kenji forgot the theft but Katsumata never did; talk about why we remember wrongs done to us better than wrongs we do.

a-brides-story.Historically Black Protestant: Ruth 1:16 is a picture of loyalty to a new family; how does Amir show the same? Talk together about the age of the husband and why customs change.
a-brides-story.Atheist: Smith studies people rather than judging them; what can we learn from his approach?
a-brides-story.Agnostic: The story lets readers judge the customs themselves; which seem good to you and which do not?
a-brides-story.Nothing in particular: The village defends Amir against her own clan; what makes a family worth defending?

a-sign-of-affection.Historically Black Protestant: Itsuomi learns sign because Yuki matters to him; talk about loving your neighbor in their own language, and about the order of steps Scripture gives for marriage.
a-sign-of-affection.Atheist: Ask what helps someone communicate without taking away their choices, using Oushi and Itsuomi as examples.
a-sign-of-affection.Agnostic: Talk about what it takes for two people from different 'worlds' to really understand each other.
a-sign-of-affection.Nothing in particular: Yuki fears being a burden; talk about how to help a friend without treating them as fragile.

a-silent-voice.Historically Black Protestant: Shoya repays the money and learns sign language; is that enough, or is something more needed (Matthew 5:23-24)? Shoko and Shoya both felt like a burden: what does Psalm 139 say about a person's worth, and who could you talk to if you felt that way?
a-silent-voice.Atheist: The whole class joined the bullying but only Shoya was punished; was that fair? What should the teachers have done?
a-silent-voice.Agnostic: Some critics say the story is more about the bully than the deaf girl; whose point of view would you want to read?
a-silent-voice.Nothing in particular: Shoko keeps apologizing even when others hurt her; why might someone do that, and how can friends help? Can a person who did harm still have worth?

ajin.Historically Black Protestant: Ajin are hunted and experimented on because they are different; how does Scripture speak of the dignity of every person (Genesis 1:27)? Sato says he fights for Ajin rights; how can you tell when a just cause is being used as cover for violence?
ajin.Atheist: Kei says everyone weighs lives on a scale (ch. 43); is he right? Where would you draw the line on research that harms some people to help many?
ajin.Agnostic: If a new mind forms after an Ajin loses their head, is it the same person? What makes you you?
ajin.Nothing in particular: Kei walks away and then comes back (ch. 43-48); what changed his mind? Who in your life plays Nakano's role?

akame-ga-kill.Historically Black Protestant: The Civil Rights movement resisted injustice without assassination. How does Night Raid's way compare with Romans 12:17-21?
akame-ga-kill.Atheist: Night Raid says its killing is still murder. If no god sets the rules, what makes torture of a defeated enemy wrong?
akame-ga-kill.Agnostic: Can anyone be sure a revolution built on killing will make things better? The story does not promise it.
akame-ga-kill.Nothing in particular: The child Emperor is executed though Honest controlled him. Was that fair?

akira.Historically Black Protestant: The Great Tokyo Empire worships a child and is secretly drugged. Read Exodus 20:3-4: what makes worship true or false?
akira.Atheist: Tetsuo's followers want a god and a ruler. Why might people hand power to someone like him?
akira.Agnostic: The story never explains where Akira and Tetsuo go at the end. Is an unanswered ending satisfying or frustrating?
akira.Nothing in particular: Everyone who tries to control Akira's power loses. Is the story saying no one can be trusted with too much power?

alice-in-borderland.Historically Black Protestant: Arisu lives because his friends gave themselves for him. Talk about hope that does not give up, and where your faith says that hope comes from.
alice-in-borderland.Atheist: Mira says nothing is real. Ask how you would answer her without appealing to anything beyond this life.
alice-in-borderland.Agnostic: The Joker says he is neither God nor Devil. Ask whether the Borderlands is a place, a metaphor, or something no one can know.
alice-in-borderland.Nothing in particular: Ask why Karube, Chota and Shibuki chose to die for Arisu, and what Arisu owes them now.

all-you-need-is-kill.Historically Black Protestant: Rita gives her life so others can live. How is that like and unlike John 15:13, and what hope does the story lack that Scripture offers?
all-you-need-is-kill.Atheist: The author says the lesson is 'when you die, it's over.' How does that change the way you read a story about endless retries?
all-you-need-is-kill.Agnostic: Rita says one of them must die. Was there another way? How sure can anyone be in a choice like that?
all-you-need-is-kill.Nothing in particular: Keiji shoots himself to test the loop and the story plays it as a joke. How is real life different?

ao-haru-ride.Historically Black Protestant: Kou shut out love after his mother died; how does God meet us in grief (Psalm 147:3)? How would you want someone to treat you if they liked you, and what does respect look like in dating?
ao-haru-ride.Atheist: What helps people through loss? Is Kou's roughness love or disrespect?
ao-haru-ride.Agnostic: Futaba changed herself to keep friends; when is fitting in wise, and when does it cost too much?
ao-haru-ride.Nothing in particular: What helped Kou risk loving again? Why might Mr. Tanaka's refusal of Shuko be the caring choice?

assassination-classroom.Historically Black Protestant: Koro-sensei asks his students to kill him: what does your church teach about choosing death, and about laying down your life for others (John 15:13)? What would you want a teacher to see in you?
assassination-classroom.Atheist: Principal Asano says fear makes people strong; where does the story show him wrong? Why do the students' weapons only hurt Koro-sensei, and does that change how the violence feels?
assassination-classroom.Agnostic: Is killing one to save billions ever right? Would Irina's kisses feel different if the adult were a man?
assassination-classroom.Nothing in particular: Can someone who did terrible things really change, as the Reaper did? What does Nagisa's choice to become a teacher say about what he learned?

attack-on-titan.Historically Black Protestant: The Eldians wear armbands and live behind walls because of who their ancestors were; talk about how the story shows hatred taught to children, and how Gabi learns the people she was told were devils are people. Compare the Blouse family's forgiveness with Romans 12:19-21.
attack-on-titan.Atheist: The walls were built on a lie and a religion was used to keep people from asking questions. Ask how propaganda shaped Reiner and Gabi, and why Armin and Hange keep searching for the truth.
attack-on-titan.Agnostic: The story gives Eren, Armin and Zeke each a strong case. Ask your teen which argument they found most convincing at first, and whether their view changed by the end.
attack-on-titan.Nothing in particular: Ask whether Eren really did it for his friends, and what loyalty means when it turns into hatred of everyone else. Check that your reader is ready for very heavy violence.

bakuman.Historically Black Protestant: Mashiro works with all his heart, as Colossians 3:23 asks, but nearly breaks his health. Talk about rest as God's gift (Psalm 127:2) and about whether the girls in the story are given equal dignity.
bakuman.Atheist: Every success here comes from revision and effort. Ask what the story gets right about work, and where reviewers say it gets women wrong.
bakuman.Agnostic: The story sets the big questions aside to focus on craft. Ask whether a dream can give a life its meaning, and what it might cost.
bakuman.Nothing in particular: Mashiro keeps a promise for years. Ask whether it was wise to put love on hold for a career, and what Hiramaru, who hates hard work, adds to the story.

banana-fish.Historically Black Protestant: Ash was bought and sold as a child; compare Luke 4:18 on freedom for captives. Does Ash's violence ever become wrong even in a just fight?
banana-fish.Atheist: Eiji wants nothing from Ash; why is that the thing that changes him?
banana-fish.Agnostic: Yoshida says Ash had to pay for the lives he took; do you agree with that ending?
banana-fish.Nothing in particular: Who protected the young people in this story, and who failed them?

battle-angel-alita.Historically Black Protestant: Zalem looks like heaven but is built on the people below; compare Amos 5:24 on justice rolling down like waters. Who does Alita choose to protect, and why?
battle-angel-alita.Atheist: Alita changes bodies many times; what stays the same and makes her herself?
battle-angel-alita.Agnostic: The story never fully explains what Alita is; is it better that some questions stay open?
battle-angel-alita.Nothing in particular: Hugo's dream turns out to be a scam; how do you tell a real hope from a false one?

beastars.Historically Black Protestant: The story's laws keep herbivores and carnivores apart. Read Galatians 3:28 and Amos 5:24: what does the Bible say about walls between peoples, and what does it ask of each person's own heart?
beastars.Atheist: Legoshi cannot wish his urge away; he has to know it and choose against it. Where do your values come from when instinct pulls the other way?
beastars.Agnostic: Gohin says hunger can feel like love. How can anyone be sure what they really feel?
beastars.Nothing in particular: Haru is called names for her past. Does the story treat her fairly, and do the other characters?

beck.Historically Black Protestant: Koyuki's voice is a gift he has to practice to use; talk about the parable of the talents in Matthew 25. Ask how the peeping gags would read from the girls' side.
beck.Atheist: Ask how much of Koyuki's rise was luck and how much was work, and whether leaving school for a dream was wise.
beck.Agnostic: Saito is crude and also a kind teacher; ask whether someone can be both a bad example and a good mentor.
beck.Nothing in particular: Ryusuke's thefts put his friends in danger; ask what he owes the band and whether he is a hero.

berserk.Historically Black Protestant: Guts is the image of someone who keeps going through suffering with no visible help; compare that with the faithful endurance of Joseph or Job and talk about where hope comes from. Ask why the story shows a church that tortures people, and how the real church should answer that charge.
berserk.Atheist: The story says evil comes from human desires, not a devil. Ask whether any dream is worth what Griffith gave up, and what the inquisition arc shows about certainty turned into cruelty.
berserk.Agnostic: Fate, causality and the God Hand are never fully explained. Ask whether Guts can be free if fate is fixed, and why the story leaves that open.
berserk.Nothing in particular: This is adult reading because of the sexual violence. For an older reader, talk about Guts learning to fight for someone instead of against someone, and why the world seems to reward Griffith anyway.

billy-bat.Historically Black Protestant: In the story Jesus draws the bat when Judas asks what God looks like. Talk about how your church answers Judas's question, and how the story treats the Klan and racism.
billy-bat.Atheist: Ask how you tell a good story about history from a false claim about it.
billy-bat.Agnostic: The same drawing looks white to some and black to others. Ask whether the bat is good, evil or neither, and who decides.
billy-bat.Nothing in particular: Ask whether a child's choice to study is enough hope after everything else that happens.

black-butler.Historically Black Protestant: Read Romans 12:19 next to Ciel's revenge, and talk about who protects the children in the story and who fails them.
black-butler.Atheist: Ask whether Ciel's denial of God is a reasoned view or a reaction to trauma, and how the story could show abuse survivors without using them for effect.
black-butler.Agnostic: Is there a difference between justice and revenge here? Talk about whether loyalty that comes from appetite, like Sebastian's, can be real loyalty.
black-butler.Nothing in particular: The servants' loyalty is the warm part; talk about what Ciel gives up for revenge and whether payback ever makes things right.

black-clover.Historically Black Protestant: The Clover Kingdom ranks people by birth; compare Galatians 3:28 and James 2. Asta's power comes from a devil he befriends; how does your church think about spirits, and how is this story different?
black-clover.Atheist: Asta has no magic but still wins: what does the story say about where worth comes from? Why give halos and wings to the villain?
black-clover.Agnostic: The story borrows angels, devils and Kabbalah names without teaching any of them; what do you make of a world where those are just story parts?
black-clover.Nothing in particular: The Black Bulls are a family of misfits; who is that for you? Asta keeps proposing after a clear no: funny or not?

blade-of-the-immortal.Historically Black Protestant: Every killing here makes a new avenger; talk about Romans 12:19-21 and the Civil Rights tradition of refusing revenge. Ask whether Manji's plan to kill a thousand evil men can ever pay for a hundred good ones.
blade-of-the-immortal.Atheist: Habaki obeys the state completely and the state orders his death; ask what the story says about loyalty to institutions and who earns it.
blade-of-the-immortal.Agnostic: Rin asks whether it is worse to die without reaching your goal or to live forever without reaching it; ask what you think and why.
blade-of-the-immortal.Nothing in particular: Many survivors are the ones who stop fighting; ask what that suggests about revenge, and why Rin hides the truth from Renzo.

blame.Historically Black Protestant: Killy keeps going for ten volumes without giving up; where does a believer find the strength to endure (Isaiah 40:31)? Is ending the suffering woman's life in Log 36 mercy, or a choice that belongs to God?
blame.Atheist: Cibo moves into new bodies many times; is she still the same person? Can a system be dangerous even if no one in it means harm?
blame.Agnostic: The story explains almost nothing; what do you think the City and the Authority are? Why end with a child rather than a victory?
blame.Nothing in particular: Killy almost never speaks; what do his actions tell you about him? What gives the ending its hope?

bleach.Historically Black Protestant: Ichigo defies Soul Society to save Rukia from an unjust sentence; talk about when God's people have rightly stood against unjust rulers (Exodus 1:15-21; Acts 5:29). Ask how the story's 'god', kept in place by hidden sacrifice, compares with the God of the Bible, and why the author gave the villain God's name.
bleach.Atheist: The 'god' at the top of this world turns out to be a sealed thing kept in place by those in power. Ask what that says about authorities who claim to speak for heaven, and whether Soul Society's genocide of the Quincy was ever justified.
bleach.Agnostic: Aizen says a world without fear of death would also have no hope or courage. Ask your teen whether they agree, and what they think the story believes about death.
bleach.Nothing in particular: Ichigo's whole creed is to protect the people he loves. Ask when it is right to disobey an authority, and how you know.

blood-on-the-tracks.Historically Black Protestant: Ephesians 6 asks children to honor parents and fathers not to provoke their children; how do both halves apply to this family? Where could Seiichi have found the hope the story never names?
blood-on-the-tracks.Atheist: Seiko was not loved by her own parents; does understanding her past change how we judge what she did? What are the signs of emotional abuse, and where can a young person get help?
blood-on-the-tracks.Agnostic: Can a harm be understood without being excused? Why do you think the last conversation happens in a dream?
blood-on-the-tracks.Nothing in particular: What does a child owe a parent who did great harm? If someone you know felt as empty as adult Seiichi, who could they talk to?

bloom-into-you.Historically Black Protestant: Touko lived behind a mask to replace her sister; what does it mean to be known and loved as you are (Psalm 139)? How does this story's view of love and sex compare with what your church teaches, and how can you speak about it with both truth and kindness (Ephesians 4:15)?
bloom-into-you.Atheist: Is the self something you find or something you make? When should Touko have asked before kissing Yuu?
bloom-into-you.Agnostic: The play asks which version of a person is the real one; how would you answer? Why do readers argue so much about Yuu's feelings?
bloom-into-you.Nothing in particular: When is it good to carry on someone's legacy, and when does it cost you yourself? Sayaka is turned down; what does she do well afterward?

blue-box.Historically Black Protestant: Taiki and Chinatsu hide their relationship from his parents: when should parents be told, and why? How do you keep going when something you worked for ends, as with Chinatsu's injury?
blue-box.Atheist: What is the point of effort that may not win? Was Taiki kind or cruel in telling Hina clearly he did not return her feelings?
blue-box.Agnostic: The story ends with graduation, not a wedding: what does 'leaving the box' of youth mean to you?
blue-box.Nothing in particular: Taiki's father finds out and chooses understanding with a warning; was that the right call? What do you owe a family that takes you in?

blue-exorcist.Historically Black Protestant: Rin did not choose his father, but he chooses whom he serves (Joshua 24:15). Talk about how Fujimoto's sacrifice differs from Yukio's and Shura's attempts on their own lives, and how the story uses Bible verses.
blue-exorcist.Atheist: No god shows up to save anyone; people save each other. Ask whether the story blames religion, science or power for the Order's crimes.
blue-exorcist.Agnostic: Every tradition's rites work in this world, and none is called the truth. Ask what that says about how the author sees religion.
blue-exorcist.Nothing in particular: Rin's friends decide to trust him after learning what he is (ch. 26). Ask what you owe the family that raised you rather than the one you were born to.

blue-flag.Historically Black Protestant: Rumors about Toma spread after the culture festival (ch. 42). Talk about speaking the truth in love (Ephesians 4:15), and what your family believes about the story's ending.
blue-flag.Atheist: Ask whether the self is something you find or something you choose.
blue-flag.Agnostic: Ask where ideas of 'normal' come from and who should get to decide.
blue-flag.Nothing in particular: Ask why spreading someone's secret is harmful even if it is true.

blue-lock.Historically Black Protestant: Blue Lock says greatness comes from ego; read Philippians 2:3-4 together and ask whether a person can be humble and still want to be the best. Talk about the players who are cut and never seen again, and who looks out for them.
blue-lock.Atheist: Isagi improves by studying the game and being honest about his weaknesses. Ask whether a system is fair if 299 players lose so one can win, and whether results justify how Ego treats them.
blue-lock.Agnostic: Ego is sure he has the one right answer, and the story mostly agrees with him. Ask your child what the teamwork side would say back, and whether the story gives it a fair hearing.
blue-lock.Nothing in particular: Ask what the difference is between ambition and selfishness, and what friends owe each other when Nagi leaves Reo behind. Mention the strong language before handing it over.

blue-period.Historically Black Protestant: Yatora works heartily at his gift, as if for the Lord. How do you use your gifts well, and how do you show love to a friend like Yuka while holding to what your church teaches?
blue-period.Atheist: Yatora felt empty while succeeding at what he was handed. What makes a life feel chosen and meaningful to you?
blue-period.Agnostic: Yatora's mother wanted security and the story gives her case weight. Who was right, and can both be?
blue-period.Nothing in particular: Yuka says it is hard to be what the world tells you to be. How should friends treat each other when they see things differently?

boruto.Historically Black Protestant: Boruto keeps protecting people who believe a lie about him. How is that like Joseph in Genesis 37-50, and how does God make a way?
boruto.Atheist: The 'gods' here are aliens who feed on worlds. What does the story say people should do when someone claims to be above them?
boruto.Agnostic: If everyone remembered you wrongly, what would still make you you?
boruto.Nothing in particular: Kawaki seals Naruto and Hinata away 'to protect them.' When does love turn into control?

boys-abyss.Historically Black Protestant: Where were the church family and the elders who should have protected Reiji? Talk about how to spot grooming and where a hurting teen can find help and hope.
boys-abyss.Atheist: A story about despair is not an argument for it: what actually helps Reiji, and what only seems to? Talk about consent and how adults abuse trust.
boys-abyss.Agnostic: The story answers Reiji's pain with honesty rather than faith; what else might have helped him? Why do readers still like characters the story treats as harmful?
boys-abyss.Nothing in particular: What did Reiji owe his family, and what did they owe him? If a friend felt like Reiji, who could they talk to?

bungo-stray-dogs.Historically Black Protestant: Atsushi was told he had no right to live. Read Psalm 139:13-16 together: how does the story's answer to his worth compare with Scripture's?
bungo-stray-dogs.Atheist: Fyodor says humanity must be purified of sin. How can you tell when talk about goodness is really about control?
bungo-stray-dogs.Agnostic: Dazai keeps looking for a reason to live. Does the story ever give him one, and does it need a final answer?
bungo-stray-dogs.Nothing in particular: Dazai's wish to die is often played as a joke. Is that fair to people who really struggle with those feelings?

call-of-the-night.Historically Black Protestant: Ko stops going to school and nobody notices; who in a church family would have noticed, and what should they have done? Kiku calls what she does to Mahiru love; how does 1 Corinthians 13 help tell love from control?
call-of-the-night.Atheist: Nazuna is decades older than Ko but looks like a teenager; how does that change how you read their relationship? What helps a young person who cannot sleep and has stopped going to school?
call-of-the-night.Agnostic: Is the night in this story freedom, escape or both? Seri is happy without romance; does a full life need it?
call-of-the-night.Nothing in particular: Anko gives up her revenge; what made that possible? Is Ko's life better at the end than at the start, and why?

chained-soldier.Historically Black Protestant: Yuuki is diligent and kind: does paying his service with sexual rewards change how you see it? What does Scripture say about the eyes and the heart (Matthew 5:28)?
chained-soldier.Atheist: Kyouka's body must give the reward even if she does not want to: what does that say about consent? Who are the real monsters in the bureau storyline?
chained-soldier.Agnostic: Only women can use Peach powers and men are second-class; does the story say anything about that, or just use it as a setting?
chained-soldier.Nothing in particular: The creators say the revealing scenes are necessary; what does a story really need? Is a fair trade still fair if one side cannot refuse?

chainsaw-man.Historically Black Protestant: Denji is born into debt bondage and then into a gentler kind of slavery under Makima; ask where real freedom comes from, and compare it to Exodus and Galatians 5:1. Talk about why the story's devils are treated as friends and what Scripture says about that.
chainsaw-man.Atheist: The story finds meaning without any god: bread, a bed, friends. Ask whether Makima's promise of a world without suffering is worth giving up your freedom, and how the hero cult in Part 2 manipulates people.
chainsaw-man.Agnostic: The ending loops back to the start instead of explaining anything. Ask your teen what they think Denji learned, and whether a story has to give answers to be meaningful.
chainsaw-man.Nothing in particular: Small dreams like a warm meal and people to share it with are the happy ending here. Check the age fit first, then talk about what makes someone a real friend versus someone who just gives you what you want.

choujin-x.Historically Black Protestant: Zora believed a vision justified killing thousands (ch. 49). How does 1 John 4:1 tell believers to test a vision?
choujin-x.Atheist: Tokio and Azuma inject a drug they do not understand; what would checking the evidence first have looked like?
choujin-x.Agnostic: Can anyone be sure enough about the future to harm people now? What does the story say?
choujin-x.Nothing in particular: Tokio's power shows what he wanted most. What would yours show, and is that who you want to be?

citrus.Historically Black Protestant: Mei kisses and pins Yuzu the night they meet; talk about consent, respect for another's body (1 Corinthians 6:19-20), and how your family's teaching on marriage compares with the story's happy ending.
citrus.Atheist: Some reviewers love this story and some say it makes force look romantic; ask which scenes support each view and what consent should look like.
citrus.Agnostic: Matsuri uses a photo to force Mei into meeting a stranger; ask why blackmail is so damaging and what made her stop.
citrus.Nothing in particular: Ask why the grandfather wanted Mei to marry, what changed his mind, and whether following your heart is always right.

claymore.Historically Black Protestant: The Claymores keep protecting villagers who fear and shun them; how is that like loving those who mistreat you (Luke 6:27-28)? Is the black card mercy, or does it take a decision that belongs to God?
claymore.Atheist: Miria finds out that the Organization makes the very monsters it sells protection from; how do you tell when an authority is lying to you?
claymore.Agnostic: Teresa's spirit fights beside Clare at the end; is that meant literally, or as a picture of how the dead live on in us? Why does Rabona change its mind about the Claymores?
claymore.Nothing in particular: What keeps Clare human when her body is not? What would you say to a friend who asked you to do what the black card asks?

d-gray-man.Historically Black Protestant: The Earl preys on grief by offering the dead back. Talk about Christian hope for the dead (1 Thessalonians 4:13) and how to respond when church leaders do wrong.
d-gray-man.Atheist: Allen will not let anyone undo death. Ask why the story treats accepting loss as the moral choice.
d-gray-man.Agnostic: Innocence is called God's power, but the story never shows who God is. Ask whether an unfinished story can still say something about faith.
d-gray-man.Nothing in particular: 'Keep walking' is Allen's motto after loss. Ask what helps someone keep going, and what Allen means when he calls his friends home.

dandadan.Historically Black Protestant: Seiko is a spirit medium and the story treats her craft as good; talk about what Scripture says about mediums (Deuteronomy 18:10-12) and why your family may draw the line there. Also talk about the adults who try to exploit teens and what to do if anyone ever pressures them.
dandadan.Atheist: The story condemns people who use religion to hurt others, like the family that sacrificed children. Ask how the heroes respond to adults who try to exploit them, and whether the series uses those threats too often.
dandadan.Agnostic: Momo and Okarun each laughed at what the other believed and were both wrong. Ask what changed when they took each other seriously.
dandadan.Nothing in particular: Silky did terrible things because she lost her daughter, and the heroes help her pass on in peace. Ask whether understanding someone's pain changes how we judge what they did, and check the Mature content first.

dead-dead-demons-dededede-destruction.Historically Black Protestant: The invaders are small and helpless, yet the crowd calls for their destruction. Talk about loving the stranger and enemy (Matthew 5:44) and how the church has stood against those who stir up hatred.
dead-dead-demons-dededede-destruction.Atheist: The news in the story spins and lies. Ask how you check what you see on TV or online.
dead-dead-demons-dededede-destruction.Agnostic: Kadode wanted to save the world; Ouran chose to save one person. Ask which is better, and how anyone can be sure.
dead-dead-demons-dededede-destruction.Nothing in particular: Ask why so many people hate the invaders, and what Watarase owed Kadode as her former teacher.

deadman-wonderland.Historically Black Protestant: Ganta was framed and convicted in minutes: what makes a trial fair, and why does it matter even for the guilty? Why does Ganta refuse revenge, and what does Scripture say about it?
deadman-wonderland.Atheist: The tourists cheer because they think the deaths are fake; are readers who enjoy the gore any different? Where should science stop, and who decides?
deadman-wonderland.Agnostic: Genkaku calls death 'salvation'; how does the story answer him? Many of Ganta's friends really did kill; does the story excuse them, explain them, or something else?
deadman-wonderland.Nothing in particular: Shiro wanted to die; what does the ending say to someone who feels they should never have been born? Who could a friend in that place talk to?

death-note-a-kira.Historically Black Protestant: Minoru will not kill but sells the power to kill; compare Proverbs 1:19 on gain taken by violence. Is selling a weapon different from using it?
death-note-a-kira.Atheist: People praise Kira as a god again once they get money; why do people give that kind of trust to power?
death-note-a-kira.Agnostic: The rules change after the deal; what does the story say about how much anyone can plan for?
death-note-a-kira.Nothing in particular: Is Minoru's death fair? What would you have done with the notebook?

death-note.Historically Black Protestant: James 4:12 says there is one Lawgiver and Judge; when did Light's 'justice' stop being justice? Why might a frightened public accept a killer who promises safety, and what does Amos 5:24 say real justice looks like?
death-note.Atheist: L also lies, spies on families and locks up suspects; is he different from Light? What would due process have required?
death-note.Agnostic: Ryuk says everyone ends in nothingness; does the story need that answer, or would it work with the question left open?
death-note.Nothing in particular: If you could punish wrongdoers with no chance of being caught, would that make the world better? Did Light get what was coming to him?

delicious-in-dungeon.Historically Black Protestant: Marcille breaks the law to bring Falin back: was it love or a wrong choice made for love? Why does the story end an adventure with a shared table, and what does that echo in church life?
delicious-in-dungeon.Atheist: Senshi says waste nothing you kill: what do we owe the animals and plants we eat? How does Laios solve problems by studying how things work?
delicious-in-dungeon.Agnostic: Why does the story treat a person with no desires as harmed rather than freed? What does it mean to accept being part of the food chain?
delicious-in-dungeon.Nothing in particular: The elves treat shorter-lived races like children; where do you see that kind of prejudice? Who would you invite to your table after a fight?

demon-slayer.Historically Black Protestant: Tanjiro mourns the demons he has to stop; talk about Romans 12:21 and what it means to overcome evil with good without hating the person. Ask how the story's spirits and afterlife differ from the Christian hope of resurrection.
demon-slayer.Atheist: Muzan wants to live forever, and the story says that wish is the root of evil. Ask what makes a short life complete, and talk about why the author made the cult leader who denies every god so empty.
demon-slayer.Agnostic: The dead seem to meet the dying, and the last chapter hints at rebirth, but nothing is explained. Ask what your child thinks those scenes mean, and why the author might leave them unexplained.
demon-slayer.Nothing in particular: The heroes protect their families and keep their promises, and the dead are shown watching over them. Ask how Kagaya's and Shinobu's choices are different from giving up on life.

domestic-girlfriend.Historically Black Protestant: Hina was Natsuo's teacher and had authority over him. Talk about why Scripture and the law ask adults to protect the young, and what real love does for a 17-year-old.
domestic-girlfriend.Atheist: Ask who held the power when the relationship began, and whether a minor can consent to an adult in authority.
domestic-girlfriend.Agnostic: Reviewers read the same story as a warning and as an excuse. Ask which reading the ending supports.
domestic-girlfriend.Nothing in particular: Rui steps aside at the end. Ask whether that is love, sacrifice or something else, and what fair consequences for Hina would have been.

dont-toy-with-me-miss-nagatoro.Historically Black Protestant: Nagatoro makes Senpai cry in chapter one. Is that love? Compare it with 1 Corinthians 13 and Ephesians 4:29, and talk about why the church teaches purity and honoring one another in dating.
dont-toy-with-me-miss-nagatoro.Atheist: Would the early scenes read differently if a boy did these things to a girl? What makes teasing playful versus harmful, and what does consent mean here?
dont-toy-with-me-miss-nagatoro.Agnostic: The story starts with teasing as affection and ends with honesty. Does the ending make up for how it began?
dont-toy-with-me-miss-nagatoro.Nothing in particular: Senpai lies to Nagatoro and nearly loses her. Why does the story treat honesty as so important, and when does teasing stop being a joke?

dorohedoro.Historically Black Protestant: In this story devils run the world and becoming one is a promotion; how does that compare with Ephesians 6:12 and what your church teaches about evil? The Hole's dead want revenge on all sorcerers: is that justice, and what does Romans 12:19 say?
dorohedoro.Atheist: Does the comedy change how we judge the heroes' killing? Who holds power in the Hole, and why?
dorohedoro.Agnostic: Why might an author make the devils bored and silly rather than frightening?
dorohedoro.Nothing in particular: Why might the author end a blood-soaked story with a restaurant reopening? Caiman learns he is several people and still chooses one name: what makes you who you are?

dr-stone.Historically Black Protestant: Psalm 19:1 says the heavens declare the glory of God; is Senku's science a gift from the Creator or a rival savior? Byakuya left his son survival knowledge in the village tales: what has your family or church passed down to you?
dr-stone.Atheist: Is there anything science cannot answer? Senku and Xeno are both geniuses: what makes one a hero and the other a would-be dictator?
dr-stone.Agnostic: Does explaining a tradition make it less valuable, or more?
dr-stone.Nothing in particular: Tsukasa wants a world without greedy adults; what is right in his anger, and what is wrong in his plan? Why does Senku insist on reviving even his enemies?

dragon-ball-super.Historically Black Protestant: The gods here sulk, eat and destroy on a whim; talk about how that differs from the God of the Bible who acts in history for the oppressed. Ask what Vegeta owes after admitting his people did terrible things.
dragon-ball-super.Atheist: Zeno can erase a universe like a child knocking over blocks; ask whether power alone makes anyone worth obeying.
dragon-ball-super.Agnostic: Ask whether Goku was right to summon Zeno knowing a whole timeline might vanish, and who gets to decide such things.
dragon-ball-super.Nothing in particular: Android 17 could have wished for anything and chose to save others; ask why, and whether Granolah's revenge would have been fair.

dragon-ball.Historically Black Protestant: Vegeta changes over many years and finally gives his life for his family: what changes a proud heart? How would Roshi's behavior toward women be seen in real life, and what does Scripture ask of us?
dragon-ball.Atheist: If wishes can bring the dead back, does death in the story still matter? Goku trains mostly for fun; is that a good reason to work hard?
dragon-ball.Agnostic: Gods in this world can be out-trained by mortals; what does that say about where the story puts its trust? Do you think Vegeta's change is real?
dragon-ball.Nothing in particular: Gohan wants to be a scholar but keeps being needed to fight; how do you balance your dreams and duty to others? Why does Goku keep giving his enemies a second chance?

fairy-tail.Historically Black Protestant: The guild welcomes back people who once attacked it: what does repentance look like, and how does a church family receive it? Can friendship save a person by itself, or do we need more?
fairy-tail.Atheist: What makes a community worth belonging to without a shared faith? Do the big fights and the fan-service art send the same message about women?
fairy-tail.Agnostic: Fairy Tail accepts anyone who is loyal; what are the limits of acceptance? Why does Jiemma's guild fail where Fairy Tail succeeds?
fairy-tail.Nothing in particular: What should someone have to do to be welcomed back after hurting you? How does Makarov show he cares, even when he expels his own grandson?

fire-force.Historically Black Protestant: Iris keeps praying after learning her church was founded on a lie; how is that like keeping faith in God when people in the church fail you? In the finale a human remakes the world; how does that compare with Genesis 1?
fire-force.Atheist: How did the Holy Sol Temple use belief to make people accept their fate? Is Tamaki's 'Lucky Lecher Lure' funny, harmful, or both?
fire-force.Agnostic: Shinra says faith has value whatever its object; do you agree? Why does the story save the sincere believer but condemn the institution?
fire-force.Nothing in particular: Shinra is called a devil by people he protects; why keep helping them? What does Company 8 do that makes it feel like a family?

fire-punch.Historically Black Protestant: The freed slaves want a god so badly that they make one out of Agni; how is that different from the God who heard Israel's cry in Exodus 3:7? Agni finds Doma changed; what does Romans 12:19 say about leaving vengeance to God?
fire-punch.Atheist: Togata says religion works because it controls crowds; is that the whole story about why people believe? Does showing this much abuse help readers understand evil or use victims for shock?
fire-punch.Agnostic: Is the story fair to Sun's sincere faith, or does it treat all belief as a trick?
fire-punch.Nothing in particular: Luna tells Agni to 'live on'; is that a gift or a burden? Togata hides pain behind jokes: how can friends tell when someone is hurting?

fly-me-to-the-moon.Historically Black Protestant: Nasa and Tsukasa commit first and learn love through daily care. Talk about what makes a marriage strong, and what your family believes someone should know before saying 'I do'.
fly-me-to-the-moon.Atheist: Nasa tries to understand immortality with science. Ask whether living forever would be a gift or a burden.
fly-me-to-the-moon.Agnostic: Ask what gives life meaning if it never ends, and whether some questions are better left open.
fly-me-to-the-moon.Nothing in particular: Tokiko's will asks Nasa to stay by Tsukasa no matter what. Ask what it means to make a home with someone.

food-wars.Historically Black Protestant: Erina is freed from a father who controlled her. How does the story show deliverance, and what does Philippians 4:8 say about the reaction pages along the way?
food-wars.Atheist: Azami says there is one right way to cook. How does the story test that claim?
food-wars.Agnostic: Who gets to decide what is 'good'? The story says the customer in front of you. Do you agree?
food-wars.Nothing in particular: Soma loses many times and shrugs it off. Why might that be a strength?

fruits-basket.Historically Black Protestant: The Sohmas are freed from a bondage held in place by fear; talk about deliverance in Exodus and Galatians 5:1, and ask whether Rin has to forgive Akito or go back to her.
fruits-basket.Atheist: The family's god is a frightened person; ask how people end up obeying someone who hurts them, and what finally breaks the hold.
fruits-basket.Agnostic: Akito was abused by her own mother; ask whether that changes how we judge what she did, and whether understanding is the same as excusing.
fruits-basket.Nothing in particular: Tohru helps everyone but hides her own feelings; ask when kindness becomes a way of avoiding yourself, and talk through how the story presents Kyoko's romance with her teacher.

fullmetal-alchemist.Historically Black Protestant: The Ishvalans are a faithful people nearly wiped out by the state, and the story honors their restoration. Compare their story with the Exodus, and ask why trying to become God is treated as the deepest evil.
fullmetal-alchemist.Atheist: Edward tells Rose the dead do not come back and exposes Cornello's fake miracles with evidence. Yet Father's science without ethics becomes a horror. What should limit what science may do?
fullmetal-alchemist.Agnostic: The story shows a fake religion, a sincere persecuted faith and a mysterious being called Truth. How does it tell sincere faith from manipulation?
fullmetal-alchemist.Nothing in particular: At the end Edward says he will give more than he takes. Is that fairer than equivalent exchange, and how could you live that way?

gachiakuta.Historically Black Protestant: Rudo is judged by who his father was; how does Scripture answer that (Ezekiel 18:20)? He wants revenge at first; what does Romans 12:19 say about leaving justice to God?
gachiakuta.Atheist: The Sphere decides people's worth by their birth; what should decide it instead? Can anger at injustice be turned into something useful?
gachiakuta.Agnostic: Why do the cherished objects in the story have power? What things in your life feel like they carry part of the person who gave them to you?
gachiakuta.Nothing in particular: Rudo, the Raiders and the Cleaners all respond to the same unfairness; which response seems best to you? Amo hurt others after being hurt herself; how can someone be both a victim and responsible?

gantz.Historically Black Protestant: In chapter 1 only Kato jumps down to help the man on the tracks. Compare that with the Good Samaritan. The beings say there is no God and humans are like ants; how does Psalm 8 answer that?
gantz.Atheist: If the universe does not care about us, does it follow that nothing we do matters? How do Kurono and Kato answer that without any god?
gantz.Agnostic: The beings behind Gantz claim total certainty about God and souls. Is their certainty any more justified than a believer's? How would anyone know?
gantz.Nothing in particular: Sakurai breaks down after killing a giant child. Does it matter that the enemy has families too, and what makes a life worth something?

girls-last-tour.Historically Black Protestant: In the temple, Chito says people built such places to feel at ease about death: what does your church say about why we pray and what we hope for? Why did the girls return what they took from the graves?
girls-last-tour.Atheist: Did the girls' journey matter if no one will ever know about it? Chito records everything and Yuuri forgets; which way of living do you lean toward?
girls-last-tour.Agnostic: What do you think happens at the end, and why might the author leave it open? What would make a life 'count' for you?
girls-last-tour.Nothing in particular: Yuuri throws her rifle away near the end; what does that say about the world they came from? What small joys make a hard day good?

given.Historically Black Protestant: The band helps Mafuyu sing his grief instead of hiding it, as the Psalms do. Talk about how a church family comforts someone after a suicide, and what your church teaches about the romances.
given.Atheist: Ask whether art can turn a loss into something worthwhile, and what the story says should happen after someone causes harm.
given.Agnostic: Ask what the difference is between love and dependence, using Akihiko and Ugetsu.
given.Nothing in particular: Mafuyu blames himself for one sentence. Ask what you would tell a friend who felt the same.

goblin-slayer.Historically Black Protestant: Psalm 82:3-4 calls for rescuing the weak and needy; who does that here, and at what cost? Talk about the bath scenes with the 15-year-old and the pagan miracles before deciding.
goblin-slayer.Atheist: The rookies die because they did not prepare; what does the story say about skill versus luck?
goblin-slayer.Agnostic: Priestess asks whether a good goblin could exist; why does that question matter even inside a fantasy?
goblin-slayer.Nothing in particular: Goblin Slayer is pulled back into life by friends; who keeps you from shutting the world out?

gokurakugai.Historically Black Protestant: Tao takes in a boy no one else would claim; talk about adoption into God's family (Romans 8:15) and why the church calls caring for the fatherless holy work. Ask how the story treats beastmen who are pushed to the bottom.
gokurakugai.Atheist: Alma is human because of how he acts, not what he was born as. Ask where goodness comes from if not from blood or a god.
gokurakugai.Agnostic: The story borrows the words Paradise, Yomi and karma without saying any of them are true. Ask why an author might name a place of misery Paradise.
gokurakugai.Nothing in particular: Tao is family to Alma without being his parent. Ask what makes someone family, and whether Kanata could have been saved.

golden-kamuy.Historically Black Protestant: Why does Asirpa refuse to let the gold pay for anyone's war, and what does that say about a people's future? Tsurumi's anger at the government has real causes; where does a fair grievance turn into something wrong?
golden-kamuy.Atheist: Sugimoto has killed many people; what makes him a hero anyway, if he is one? When is it fine to laugh at evil in a story, and when is it not?
golden-kamuy.Agnostic: Every faction thinks its cause justifies taking the gold; how does the story judge them? What does loyalty to a nation ask of a person, and where should it stop?
golden-kamuy.Nothing in particular: Asirpa thanks the animals she hunts; how does your family think about where food comes from? Why does keeping a promise to a dead friend matter so much to Sugimoto?

goodbye-eri.Historically Black Protestant: 1 Thessalonians 4:13 speaks of grieving with hope; where does Yuta's hope come from, and where would yours? Yuta first plans to die so bullies will remember him: who stopped him, and who could you talk to if you ever felt that way?
goodbye-eri.Atheist: Yuta's father says we can decide how we remember someone; when is that kind, and when does it become untrue?
goodbye-eri.Agnostic: The ending leaves it unclear what is real; does it matter to you, and why?
goodbye-eri.Nothing in particular: Eri's friend says the movie version of Eri was too perfect; do we do this with people we love, or with ourselves online? Why do you think Yuta added an explosion to his mother's film?

goodnight-punpun.Historically Black Protestant: This is adult reading. With an older reader, talk about which adults failed Punpun and Aiko, and how a church family is meant to catch children like them (Psalm 68:5-6). Make sure they know that despair is not the end of the story for a believer, and where to find help.
goodnight-punpun.Atheist: No god and no grand cause saves anyone here; a friend and a job do. Ask why the cults in the story offer such false hope, and what real help would have looked like for Punpun.
goodnight-punpun.Agnostic: The author says none of the world's values are simply right. Ask whether your teen agrees, and whether an ending without answers felt honest or empty.
goodnight-punpun.Nothing in particular: This is a heavy story about depression and abuse, best for adults. If an older teen reads it, ask who could have helped Punpun, and make sure they know who they could talk to.

grand-blue-dreaming.Historically Black Protestant: The club often makes people drink after they say no. What does Scripture say about drunkenness (Ephesians 5:18), and what does real friendship look like without pressure?
grand-blue-dreaming.Atheist: Binge drinking is the main joke here. Is it still funny if it happened in real life? What does the evidence say about alcohol poisoning?
grand-blue-dreaming.Agnostic: Why do you think the characters who stay sober are often the ones embarrassed? Whose view does the story leave out?
grand-blue-dreaming.Nothing in particular: The friends are loyal but also pushy. Can a group be both? How would you say no to a friend and stay friends?

gto-great-teacher-onizuka.Historically Black Protestant: Onizuka breaks laws to help his students: when, if ever, does a good result excuse the method? What does Scripture ask of teachers and elders who are trusted with children?
gto-great-teacher-onizuka.Atheist: What makes a teacher good: credentials, care, or both? Why might readers today react differently to the jokes about an adult's attraction to students?
gto-great-teacher-onizuka.Agnostic: How should a school handle an accusation it cannot yet prove, as with Miyabi's? When should a rule give way to a person's need?
gto-great-teacher-onizuka.Nothing in particular: Several students want to give up and are rescued; what actually helped them? Who are the adults you would go to if a friend was in trouble?

haikyu.Historically Black Protestant: Paul says the body has many parts (1 Corinthians 12); how does Karasuno show that? Ennoshita once quit and was welcomed back; compare Peter's restoration in John 21.
haikyu.Atheist: What actually makes Hinata better: talent, practice or the team? Was Takeda right to pull him with a fever?
haikyu.Agnostic: Oikawa and Ushijima each believe something different about talent and work; who is right, or are both partly right?
haikyu.Nothing in particular: Can you want to win and still be humble? Tsukishima says 'it's just a club': what changed his mind?

hajime-no-ippo.Historically Black Protestant: Ippo learns to fight but never uses it on the boys who bullied him; talk about strength under control and Romans 12:19 on leaving revenge to God. Ask how the gym works like a church family when someone falls.
hajime-no-ippo.Atheist: Ippo's retirement rests on what a doctor cannot rule out; talk about weighing evidence about risk to your own body, and whether a sport aimed at the head should be celebrated.
hajime-no-ippo.Agnostic: Takamura says winning at the top means leaving your humanity behind; ask whether that is true and what the story seems to think.
hajime-no-ippo.Nothing in particular: Ask what Ippo owes his mother, his trainer and his pupil, and why he tries to turn himself in when nobody reported him.

hells-paradise.Historically Black Protestant: The Tensen offer a paradise built on others' suffering; how can you tell a true hope from a false one (1 John 4:1)? Nurugai is condemned only for who her people are: what does Scripture say about God's care for the stranger (Deuteronomy 10:18-19)?
hells-paradise.Atheist: Why does the story reject living forever? Can a person trained to feel nothing be rehumanized?
hells-paradise.Agnostic: Sagiri's power grows when she accepts her doubt instead of hiding it; what does that say about certainty?
hells-paradise.Nothing in particular: Gabimaru says he cannot die because he wants to see his wife again; what gives a person a reason to live? When does love become harmful, as with Rien?

homunculus.Historically Black Protestant: Nakoshi tries to make himself a new face with money, surgery and lies. Compare that with being made new in Christ (2 Corinthians 5:17), and talk about why using someone 'to save them' is not love.
homunculus.Atheist: Ito runs an experiment on a person for money and then reveals a placebo. What makes research on people ethical, and how would you test whether Nakoshi's visions are real?
homunculus.Agnostic: Is the ending, where every face is Nakoshi's own, a kind of peace or a kind of prison? Can anyone know what he really saw?
homunculus.Nothing in particular: The yakuza boss finds peace by confessing; Nakoshi never does. What makes the difference between them?

horimiya.Historically Black Protestant: Miyamura felt that nobody needed him; talk about how God sees the lonely (Psalm 68:6) and what a church family could have done for him. Discuss Hori and Miyamura sleeping together as high schoolers, and what your family teaches about waiting for marriage.
horimiya.Atheist: No one in the story helps Miyamura but his friends. Ask what an adult in his life could have done, and whether the story is right that being known by others is what heals.
horimiya.Agnostic: Everyone here has a school self and a home self. Ask your teen who knows both of theirs, and how you can tell what someone is really like.
horimiya.Nothing in particular: Ask whether readers would react differently if a boy hit a girl the way Hori hits Miyamura. Talk about what your family thinks about teen relationships and sex before your child reads the middle volumes.

hunter-x-hunter.Historically Black Protestant: Netero says humans carry a bottomless malice in their hearts; compare that with Jeremiah 17:9 and talk about where the hope of change comes from. Ask when Gon's loyalty turned into revenge, and why Scripture leaves vengeance to God.
hunter-x-hunter.Atheist: A monster becomes more humane and a boy hero becomes frightening. Ask what makes someone human, and whether the Poor Man's Rose was courage or cruelty.
hunter-x-hunter.Agnostic: The story never tells you who the good side was. Ask your teen who they sided with during the Chimera Ant arc and whether that changed by the end.
hunter-x-hunter.Nothing in particular: Killua leaves a family that trained him to kill and chooses his friends. Ask when it is right to break with family, and talk about why Hisoka is creepy rather than cool.

i-am-a-hero.Historically Black Protestant: Hideo is supposed to protect Hiromi. Talk about what Scripture asks of adults toward the young, and whether surviving is the same as living well.
i-am-a-hero.Atheist: A reviewer called the Hideo-Hiromi scene 'underage sex'. Ask why harm-based ethics treats an adult's relationship with a teenager differently.
i-am-a-hero.Agnostic: Kurusu's followers call him the Prophet. Ask what makes people follow someone who claims all the answers.
i-am-a-hero.Nothing in particular: Hideo ends alone, alive and calm. Ask whether that is a good life and what a good life needs.

ichi-the-witch.Historically Black Protestant: Psalm 68:6 says God sets the lonely in families; how does Ichi find a family? Talk about how your family handles 'witch' as a job title in fantasy.
ichi-the-witch.Atheist: A kingdom is kept happy by erasing its sorrow; why does the story say that is wrong?
ichi-the-witch.Agnostic: Ichi lives by a simple rule of death for death; why might the author call that dangerous?
ichi-the-witch.Nothing in particular: Desscaras makes Ichi family by choice; what makes someone family to you?

innocent.Historically Black Protestant: Charles serves an unjust system he believes God opposes; talk about the prophets who confronted kings and what faithfulness looks like when you cannot leave. Ask whether a story can condemn cruelty while dwelling on it.
innocent.Atheist: Charles grounds his objection in God, but the story's hope is reform and medicine; ask what reasons a person without faith would give against the death penalty.
innocent.Agnostic: The most loved character enjoys killing while the hero holds to mercy; ask why readers prefer her and what that says about what we admire.
innocent.Nothing in particular: Ask whether Charles is responsible for executions he was forced into at 14, and what it means to keep your conscience when your family demands otherwise.

inside-mari.Historically Black Protestant: Galatians 6:2 asks us to bear one another's burdens; how does Yori do that for Mari? Talk about why the book's sexual scenes involving a teen are a line for your family.
inside-mari.Atheist: The 'body swap' turns out to have a psychological cause; how does finding the real explanation help Mari heal?
inside-mari.Agnostic: Can anyone fully know another person from the outside? What does Yori notice that others miss?
inside-mari.Nothing in particular: Mari's mother changed her name; how much of who we are comes from family? Families will want to read this one before any teen does.

insomniacs-after-school.Historically Black Protestant: Psalm 4:8 speaks of lying down in peace; where do Ganta and Isaki find peace, and where would your family look? Ephesians 6:1-3 beside Isaki's grounding: what did she owe her parents?
insomniacs-after-school.Atheist: The scary legend turns out to be made up; why do people pass on stories like that? What gives the two leads courage without any promise of an afterlife?
insomniacs-after-school.Agnostic: Isaki fears she may not wake up; how do people live with questions no one can answer for certain?
insomniacs-after-school.Nothing in particular: Who stood by Ganta and Isaki when things got hard? When should a teen bring an adult in on a problem like insomnia?

jagaaan.Historically Black Protestant: The frogs feed on whatever people want most. Read James 1:14-15 together: how does the story picture desire growing into ruin, and where does it fall short of hope?
jagaaan.Atheist: Jagasaki starts by enjoying the violence and ends fighting for others. Can doing the right thing for the wrong reasons still be right?
jagaaan.Agnostic: If a frog showed what you wanted most, would you want to know? Why might the story leave so much unexplained?
jagaaan.Nothing in particular: Jagasaki is bored by the life everyone expects of him. Is that ordinary life really the problem?

jojo-battle-tendency.Historically Black Protestant: Joseph defends Smokey in ch. 1 and 3; talk about that, about Caesar's sacrifice and John 15:13, and about how the art draws Smokey and whether that is fair.
jojo-battle-tendency.Atheist: Ask whether wit is a kind of courage, and why the story never weighs what the Nazis it uses actually stood for.
jojo-battle-tendency.Agnostic: Is Joseph's bluffing the same as lying? Talk about when a trick is fair.
jojo-battle-tendency.Nothing in particular: Caesar dies to give Joseph a chance; talk about what we owe people who sacrifice for us, and whether one good act redeems Stroheim's early cruelty.

jojo-diamond-is-unbreakable.Historically Black Protestant: Talk about how the whole town brings Kira down, and about Amos 5:24 and justice for Reimi; then about where your family stands on ghosts and spirits in stories.
jojo-diamond-is-unbreakable.Atheist: Araki says true strength is not doing bad things; ask whether courage is just choosing not to do harm.
jojo-diamond-is-unbreakable.Agnostic: Kira wants only a quiet, untroubled life; ask why the story treats that wish as the root of his evil.
jojo-diamond-is-unbreakable.Nothing in particular: Josuke can heal anything but cannot bring back the dead; talk about what we can and cannot fix, and why Yukako's kind of love is not love.

jojo-golden-wind.Historically Black Protestant: Bucciarati disobeys his boss to protect Trish. Talk about when it is right to disobey, and whether you can change a corrupt group from inside without becoming part of it.
jojo-golden-wind.Atheist: Araki says fate cannot be changed. Ask whether you agree, and whether a 'sense of righteousness' is enough without fair institutions.
jojo-golden-wind.Agnostic: Ask whether Diavolo's endless punishment is justice, and who should decide.
jojo-golden-wind.Nothing in particular: Ask whether Fugo was a coward or prudent when he chose not to follow.

jojo-jojolion.Historically Black Protestant: Araki asks whether children inherit their parents' sins; how does Ezekiel 18:20 answer that? The curse is broken by someone paying with a life; how is that like and unlike what Christ did (Galatians 3:13)?
jojo-jojolion.Atheist: If you lost all your memories, would you still be you? What does the family's superstition about the curse cost them?
jojo-jojolion.Agnostic: Is the curse in the story spiritual, psychological or something else? Yasuho calls the ending hope despite many deaths; do you agree?
jojo-jojolion.Nothing in particular: Kaato and Jobin harm others to save their own children; where are the limits of family loyalty? Is there anything in real life that, like the Locacaca, always takes something in return?

jojo-phantom-blood.Historically Black Protestant: Dio's name means 'god' and he wants to rise above being human (ch. 11). Read Philippians 2:5-8: how is Jonathan's path the opposite of Dio's?
jojo-phantom-blood.Atheist: Jonathan wins by training and friends, not magic gifts. What does the story say makes being human worth keeping?
jojo-phantom-blood.Agnostic: Dio chooses power over his humanity. What would you have to give up, and what would you gain?
jojo-phantom-blood.Nothing in particular: Jonathan cries for Dio after beating him (ch. 42). Why might a good person mourn an enemy?

jojo-stardust-crusaders.Historically Black Protestant: Talk about John 15:13 and the friends who die for each other, then about tarot and fortune-telling in stories, and how the people of India and Egypt are drawn.
jojo-stardust-crusaders.Atheist: Ask whether knowledge or power defeated Dio, and why people follow someone who offers them power over fear.
jojo-stardust-crusaders.Agnostic: Polnareff gets his revenge; talk about whether the story treats revenge as justice.
jojo-stardust-crusaders.Nothing in particular: Jotaro crosses the world for his mother; talk about what we owe the people we love, and how the places along the route are shown.

jojo-steel-ball-run.Historically Black Protestant: Acts 8:18-24 shows Simon trying to buy the Spirit's power; how is Valentine like him? How does this story's picture of Jesus differ from what your church teaches about the empty tomb?
jojo-steel-ball-run.Atheist: Can Johnny's growth from 'minus to zero' stand without the Corpse? Valentine says whoever takes the napkin first sets the rules: is he right about power?
jojo-steel-ball-run.Agnostic: Why might an author borrow a holy figure without naming him? Does leaving it unclear make the story more or less respectful?
jojo-steel-ball-run.Nothing in particular: Araki says Valentine's love of country could be just; where does he cross the line? The Saint says not to shoot when your heart wavers: does Johnny listen?

jojo-stone-ocean.Historically Black Protestant: Pucci quotes Scripture but serves DIO. How do we tell a true shepherd from a false one (Matthew 7:15-20)? And how does God's plan differ from Pucci's 'fate' that leaves no room for choice?
jojo-stone-ocean.Atheist: Pucci says knowing your future would make everyone happy. Would it? What would you lose if every choice were already settled?
jojo-stone-ocean.Agnostic: Pucci is completely certain about God's will. What does the story suggest about people who claim to know the final answers?
jojo-stone-ocean.Nothing in particular: Jolyne gives her life for Emporio, and the world is reset afterward. Was her sacrifice still worth it?

jujutsu-kaisen-0.Historically Black Protestant: Geto dresses as a monk to take people's money and calls ordinary people 'monkeys.' How can we tell a true shepherd from a false one, and why does Scripture warn against seeking power from the dead?
jujutsu-kaisen-0.Atheist: Yuta once wanted to die and later chooses to live for his friends. What changed for him, and who can a young person talk to when they feel that way?
jujutsu-kaisen-0.Agnostic: Gojo says no curse is more twisted than love. When can love become harmful, and how is healthy love different?
jujutsu-kaisen-0.Nothing in particular: The twist is that Yuta would not let Rika go. What helps people let go of someone who has died while still remembering them?

jujutsu-kaisen.Historically Black Protestant: Yuji's grandfather tells him to help people; ask how that compares with Micah 6:8 and with laying down your life for friends. Talk about why the heroes' power comes from curses and spirits, and where your family draws the line on spells in fiction.
jujutsu-kaisen.Atheist: Curses here come from human hatred and fear, not from devils. Ask whether the higher-ups were right to sentence one boy to death to keep others safe, and why the cult that cheers a girl's death is shown as monstrous.
jujutsu-kaisen.Agnostic: Sukuna, Mahito and Geto each argue a different answer to what life is for. Ask which argument felt strongest, and why the story answers them with Yuji's actions instead of a speech.
jujutsu-kaisen.Nothing in particular: Ask what it means to die surrounded by people, and why so many characters care more about their friends than about winning. Check the age fit first; the deaths are frequent and graphic.

kagurabachi.Historically Black Protestant: Chihiro wants to kill the men who murdered his father. Read Romans 12:17-21: what would overcoming evil with good look like for him? Notice how the story treats the people sold at auction.
kagurabachi.Atheist: In chapter 72 the 'bloodthirsty savages' turn out to have been ordinary people. Why do nations tell simple stories about their wars, and how would you find out the truth?
kagurabachi.Agnostic: Is Chihiro's goal justice, revenge, or both? Who should have the right to punish his father's killers?
kagurabachi.Nothing in particular: Chihiro learns his father's swords were used for terrible things. What do we owe for the wrongs our parents did?

kaguya-sama-love-is-war.Historically Black Protestant: Shirogane works for everything he has, and Ishigami is punished for doing the right thing until his friends stand up for him; talk about Micah 6:8 and standing with the falsely accused. Discuss the later volumes' teen sexual relationship and what your family teaches about waiting.
kaguya-sama-love-is-war.Atheist: Every clever scheme fails where one honest sentence works. Ask why being honest is so hard for two of the smartest students in school.
kaguya-sama-love-is-war.Agnostic: Kaguya's family wants her to play a role; she chooses her own life. Ask when it is right to go against what your family wants, and how you would decide.
kaguya-sama-love-is-war.Nothing in particular: Ask what makes a family good: Kaguya's is rich but cold, Shirogane's poor but warm. Check the later volumes before a younger teen reads them.

kaiju-no-8.Historically Black Protestant: Kafka was told he was too old; who in Scripture was called late (Abraham, Moses)? How does the Defense Force treat Kafka when it fears him, and what would justice look like?
kaiju-no-8.Atheist: Kafka's knowledge of kaiju anatomy wins the exam; how does practical skill compare with raw talent? Is it right to keep a thinking kaiju as a weapon?
kaiju-no-8.Agnostic: The warrior spirits appear only at the end; what do you make of a mostly scientific world with a ghostly finale?
kaiju-no-8.Nothing in particular: Kafka says it is not wrong to give up, but wrong to lie to yourself; what does that mean for you? How should we treat a parent who is strict but loving?

kimi-ni-todoke.Historically Black Protestant: Read James 3 on the tongue next to the rumors about Sawako and Ayane; then talk about the last volume and when your family believes that kind of commitment belongs.
kimi-ni-todoke.Atheist: Ask why the class believed the rumors about Sawako and what evidence changed their minds.
kimi-ni-todoke.Agnostic: Kurumi tried to win by tricking people and was forgiven; talk about why Sawako forgave her.
kimi-ni-todoke.Nothing in particular: Sawako's friends stand by her when others won't; talk about how to be that kind of friend, and about Pin's refusal of Ayane as an adult keeping a boundary.

kingdom.Historically Black Protestant: Xin rises from slavery to general. Compare his rise with Joseph's, and ask whether peace can be built by conquest, or only by God's justice (Isaiah 2:4; Amos 5:24).
kingdom.Atheist: Ying Zheng believes in the 'light' in human beings and Huan Yi believes the world runs on contempt. What in the story supports each view?
kingdom.Agnostic: The story is sure that unifying China by war is right. Historians long called the First Emperor a tyrant. Should a story be this certain, and what would the conquered say?
kingdom.Nothing in particular: Why does Xin refuse to harm civilians when others in his own army do? Why do so many readers still love Huan Yi?

komi-cant-communicate.Historically Black Protestant: 1 Corinthians 13:4 says love is patient and kind; how does Tadano show that, and how is Yamai's 'love' different? Who is the quiet person in your youth group that no one notices?
komi-cant-communicate.Atheist: Komi gets better through friends, not a counselor; when should someone with anxiety get help from an adult or professional?
komi-cant-communicate.Agnostic: Komi's classmates think she is cool when she is really afraid; how often do we judge people from the outside?
komi-cant-communicate.Nothing in particular: What is the difference between helping someone and trying to fix them? Was Komi right to forgive Yamai so fast?

kubo-wont-let-me-be-invisible.Historically Black Protestant: God looks on the heart, and Kubo sees the boy everyone overlooks. Ask who is 'invisible' at school or church, and what your family thinks about dating in high school.
kubo-wont-let-me-be-invisible.Atheist: Shiraishi becomes confident because people notice him. Ask what helps a shy person grow, and when teasing stops being kind.
kubo-wont-let-me-be-invisible.Agnostic: Ask what it means to exist for other people, and whether being seen is something we give or earn.
kubo-wont-let-me-be-invisible.Nothing in particular: Ask whether Kubo listens when Shiraishi is uncomfortable, and how his friends help him find his courage.

land-of-the-lustrous.Historically Black Protestant: The Lunarians want to stop existing; Christian hope is resurrection and new life. Compare Phos's attempt to engineer salvation with grace received, and talk about where to turn when despair comes.
land-of-the-lustrous.Atheist: Phos's body is replaced piece by piece. If every part can change, what makes a person the same person, without appealing to a soul?
land-of-the-lustrous.Agnostic: The story borrows a real religion's idea of salvation and then asks whether it is good. Is nothingness a release or a loss, and can anyone know?
land-of-the-lustrous.Nothing in particular: Kongo hides the truth to protect the gems. When is keeping a secret an act of love, and when does it hurt the people you love?

liar-game.Historically Black Protestant: Nao keeps freeing people from debt they never chose; talk about the year of Jubilee in Leviticus 25 and why it matters to set captives free. Ask whether Nao's lies to stop cheaters fit Matthew 10:16.
liar-game.Atheist: Harimoto's followers believed him at their lowest moments; ask how cold reading works and how you can tell manipulation from real care.
liar-game.Agnostic: Akiyama says to believe people is to doubt them; ask what he means and whether you agree.
