liar-game.Nothing in particular: Yokoya's team turns on him; ask what that says about ruling by fear, and whether Nao's father was right to put her in the game without telling her.

look-back.Historically Black Protestant: Fujino blames herself for her friend's death; what would you say to her, and where does a believer find comfort in grief (2 Corinthians 1:3-4)? What do you make of the voice she hears at the end?
look-back.Atheist: Why does Fujino keep drawing after a senseless loss? The publisher changed how the attacker was described; was that the right decision?
look-back.Agnostic: Is the alternate timeline real, a dream, or something else? Does the story need to decide?
look-back.Nothing in particular: Fujino first draws to be the best; why does she keep drawing later? How do we honor people we have lost in our daily lives?

made-in-abyss.Historically Black Protestant: Bondrewd says he loves the children he uses: how does Scripture tell love from control? What does your church teach about ending a life to stop suffering?
made-in-abyss.Atheist: Bondrewd shows how 'progress' can excuse cruelty; what limits should research respect? Why might how a story draws children matter, apart from what happens?
made-in-abyss.Agnostic: The story will not say whether killing Mitty was right; what do you think, and why? Is any dream worth what Riko pays?
made-in-abyss.Nothing in particular: When is following your dream brave, and when is it reckless? What should never be traded for what you want?

magi.Historically Black Protestant: Morgiana turns her shackles into weapons. Read Exodus 20:2 together: what is the difference between being freed and choosing to live free?
magi.Atheist: Sinbad's plan would bring peace by taking away choice. Why does the story think freedom is worth the cost?
magi.Agnostic: The story calls fate a cage. Is a plan for your life always a cage, or only when someone forces it?
magi.Nothing in particular: Aladdin and Alibaba refuse to hate even their enemies. What does hatred do to people in this story?

maid-sama.Historically Black Protestant: Misaki carries her family like many young people in our churches do; talk about Colossians 3:23, and set 1 Corinthians 13:5 (love does not insist on its own way) beside Usui's pursuit.
maid-sama.Atheist: Usui kisses Misaki before she says she likes him (ch. 4); talk about how the story presents it and how you would see it in real life.
maid-sama.Agnostic: Critics disagree on whether the series challenges gender roles or reinforces them; ask which your reader thinks, and why.
maid-sama.Nothing in particular: Can you be strong and still need help? Misaki learns she can; talk about when it is right to lean on others.

march-comes-in-like-a-lion.Historically Black Protestant: Hinata says she will never regret defending a bullied friend; talk about standing up for the weak when it costs you, and how the Kawamoto home works like a church family for Rei.
march-comes-in-like-a-lion.Atheist: Rei is talented and pays his own way but is still drowning; ask why work alone was not enough and what actually helped him.
march-comes-in-like-a-lion.Agnostic: Kyoko hurt Rei for years and later admits it; ask what made her that way and whether understanding her changes how we judge her.
march-comes-in-like-a-lion.Nothing in particular: The sisters refuse to take their father back; ask whether that is unforgiveness or protecting their family, and talk about the age gap in Rei's announcement.

masamune-kuns-revenge.Historically Black Protestant: Masamune spent years planning revenge for something Aki never did; read Romans 12:17-21 and ask what he would have lost if he had gone through with it. Talk about how the girls are drawn and Philippians 4:8.
masamune-kuns-revenge.Atheist: Masamune never checked who really rejected him; ask how a single unchecked belief shaped eight years of his life.
masamune-kuns-revenge.Agnostic: Ask whether Masamune getting fit was good, and whether the reason he did it matters.
masamune-kuns-revenge.Nothing in particular: Yoshino did one cruel thing out of jealousy as a child; ask what it took for her to make it right, and how nicknames can shape a person.

mashle.Historically Black Protestant: The society in Mashle judges people by a mark on their face; how does Scripture answer that (1 Samuel 16:7; Galatians 3:28)? Innocent Zero wants to become a god; what does the Bible say about that kind of pride?
mashle.Atheist: Mash wins by strength; does that prove the society wrong, or just replace magic with muscles as the measure? What marks do real societies use to rank people?
mashle.Agnostic: Why does Mash turn down the title he worked so hard for?
mashle.Nothing in particular: Regro was told he was worthless and almost gave up; what changed for him? Who could you be that for?

memories-of-emanon.Historically Black Protestant: Emanon tells a story of life with no Creator in it; compare it with Genesis and Psalm 139 on being known before birth. Ask why a 17-year-old smoking and drinking goes without comment here.
memories-of-emanon.Atheist: Ask whether remembering everything since life began would be a gift or a burden, and what makes one ordinary night worth remembering.
memories-of-emanon.Agnostic: The story never explains why one person should carry all of life's memory; ask what reasons readers might imagine and whether the question needs an answer.
memories-of-emanon.Nothing in particular: The man never sees Emanon again but carries the night for years; ask what makes some ordinary days unforgettable.

mieruko-chan.Historically Black Protestant: Miko faces evil she cannot fight alone. Read Psalm 23:4 and Romans 8:38-39: where does a believer find courage when afraid?
mieruko-chan.Atheist: Many ghosts in the story come from human cruelty, like Zen's mother. What real-world fears might the ghosts stand for?
mieruko-chan.Agnostic: The story never explains the monsters. Is a mystery scarier, or more honest, when it stays unexplained?
mieruko-chan.Nothing in particular: Miko offers her dead father the pudding they fought over. How does your family remember people who have died?

mob-psycho-100.Historically Black Protestant: Mob refuses to be worshipped by the Psycho Helmet cult (ch. 91-97). Read Acts 14:11-15: why do Paul and Barnabas refuse worship, and why does Mob?
mob-psycho-100.Atheist: Reigen has no powers, yet his advice works. What makes advice trustworthy if it is not supernatural authority?
mob-psycho-100.Agnostic: Several groups in the story want someone to worship. What separates honest belief from a cult?
mob-psycho-100.Nothing in particular: Mob could win every fight but often does not use his power. When is it right not to use a strength you have?

monster.Historically Black Protestant: Matthew 5:44 says love your enemies: is Tenma's second surgery on Johan an example? How do hate groups recruit lonely people, and how did the church historically resist them?
monster.Atheist: Johan says death is the only equality; how would you answer him without appealing to God? Nature or nurture: who made Johan?
monster.Agnostic: The last pages leave Johan's fate open; why might the author refuse to give a final answer about evil?
monster.Nothing in particular: Was Tenma right to save the boy instead of the mayor? Eva and Lunge both change; what made the difference for them?

more-than-a-married-couple-but-not-lover.Historically Black Protestant: Read Hebrews 13:4 and ask why the story finds virginity funny, and whether it is; Jiro's restraint is a good point to start from.
more-than-a-married-couple-but-not-lover.Atheist: Talk about consent in the teasing scenes and whether a school should grade students' relationships at all.
more-than-a-married-couple-but-not-lover.Agnostic: Ask what makes a partnership good, compatibility, effort or attraction, and whether pretending to love someone can become the real thing.
more-than-a-married-couple-but-not-lover.Nothing in particular: The message is simple and kind: choose the person who knows you; talk about the fan service and whether it fits your reader's age.

mushoku-tensei.Historically Black Protestant: Zacchaeus made things right with the people he wronged (Luke 19:8). Does Rudeus ever do that for Sylphie or Eris?
mushoku-tensei.Atheist: The Man-God gives good advice that serves his own ends. How would you check advice from someone more powerful than you?
mushoku-tensei.Agnostic: The author said he did not want to impose a view on slavery. Should a story take a side?
mushoku-tensei.Nothing in particular: Rudeus works hard to become a better person. Does becoming better include facing the people he hurt?

my-broken-mariko.Historically Black Protestant: Shiino carries her friend's ashes because no one else will honor her; talk about grief, Psalm 34:18, and who in your church family a hurting friend could be brought to. Ask what signs a friend in danger might show and whom to tell.
my-broken-mariko.Atheist: Makio says the only way to see the dead is to keep living; ask what he means and how people find reasons to go on after a loss.
my-broken-mariko.Agnostic: The story never explains Mariko's last days or shows her letter; ask why the author left those questions open.
my-broken-mariko.Nothing in particular: The father is never punished; ask how that makes you feel, and who you could say thank you for staying alive to.

my-dearest-self-with-malice-aforethought.Historically Black Protestant: Eiji was treated as guilty because of his father; compare Ezekiel 18:20 on each person answering for their own deeds. Why does B1 hand the killer to the law instead of taking revenge?
my-dearest-self-with-malice-aforethought.Atheist: The story says blood does not make a killer; what does decide who we become?
my-dearest-self-with-malice-aforethought.Agnostic: Eiji did not know parts of his own mind; how sure can any of us be about who we are?
my-dearest-self-with-malice-aforethought.Nothing in particular: What goes around comes around for the real killer; does the ending feel fair to you, and what did it cost?

my-dress-up-darling.Historically Black Protestant: Job 31:1 speaks of a covenant with the eyes; Gojo looks away during fittings, but the art often does not. What is the difference between what a character does and what the artist shows? Philippians 4:8 is a good test for which pages to skip.
my-dress-up-darling.Atheist: Who decides what hobbies are 'for boys' or 'for girls'? How do media images push teens toward dieting?
my-dress-up-darling.Agnostic: Marin says to love what you love without shame: are there limits to that idea, and who sets them?
my-dress-up-darling.Nothing in particular: Gojo hid his hobby for ten years because one person mocked it; what would help someone share what they love? How should friends respond when Marin is told to lose weight?

my-hero-academia.Historically Black Protestant: Deku reaches out his hand even to Shigaraki; talk about loving your enemies (Matthew 5:44) and what it means to stand up to an unjust system without hatred. Ask whether Bakugo's apology was enough, and what repentance and repair look like.
my-hero-academia.Atheist: No one is chosen by fate here; anyone can be a hero. Ask whether a hero who is paid, ranked and famous is still a hero, and what the secret Commission killings say about who watches the watchers.
my-hero-academia.Agnostic: Shigaraki says a society that ignored a suffering child deserves to be destroyed. Ask what the story gets right about his complaint and where it says he went wrong.
my-hero-academia.Nothing in particular: Deku helps people without being asked, and his friends carry him when he can't go on. Talk about bullying and forgiveness, and whether people who do terrible things can still be saved.

my-lesbian-experience-with-loneliness.Historically Black Protestant: Kabi learns that paying to be held cannot give her what she needs; talk about where worth and identity really come from, and about getting help for depression and self-harm.
my-lesbian-experience-with-loneliness.Atheist: Ask what made a life feel worth living for Kabi, and why caring for yourself is a first step, not selfishness.
my-lesbian-experience-with-loneliness.Agnostic: Kabi thought one experience would make her 'normal'; talk about beliefs we hold about what will fix us, and how to test them.
my-lesbian-experience-with-loneliness.Nothing in particular: This is a memoir for older readers; if your teen reads it, talk about warning signs of self-harm and where to find help.

my-little-monster.Historically Black Protestant: Proverbs 18:24 speaks of a friend who sticks closer than a brother; who does that for Haru and Shizuku? Talk about why the early forced kiss is not romance.
my-little-monster.Atheist: Haru's aunt says education, language and love make us human; do you agree, and what would you add?
my-little-monster.Agnostic: Haru's family values image and power; what does the story suggest really matters instead?
my-little-monster.Nothing in particular: Shizuku keeps her career goal and still finds love; did she have to choose? What should Haru have done differently at the start?

nana.Historically Black Protestant: Hachi wants love and a home; what does Scripture say about where lasting love and security come from (Hebrews 13:4-5)? Ren's drugs came from his own boss; who is responsible for his death, and who should have protected Shin?
nana.Atheist: Shin is 15 and Reira is an adult; why do many readers call this relationship harmful even though the story shows it tenderly? What would real support for Ren have looked like?
nana.Agnostic: The story may never be finished; what ending do you think it is heading toward? Can two people save each other from loneliness?
nana.Nothing in particular: Nana loves Hachi and Ren but fears being left; how does fear change the way people love? What did the friends do well for Nana after Ren died?

naruto.Historically Black Protestant: Naruto tells Pain he cannot forgive him but will not kill him; is that the same as forgiveness (Matthew 5:44)? How do the villagers treat Naruto before they know him, and who are the outcasts in our community?
naruto.Atheist: The story says hard work beats talent, but Naruto turns out to have a special bloodline; does that change the message?
naruto.Agnostic: Pain, Itachi and Madara each have a theory of how to make peace; which is most convincing, and why does Naruto's win?
naruto.Nothing in particular: Itachi killed his family to prevent a war; can a good goal make that right? What does it take to break a cycle of revenge?

neon-genesis-evangelion.Historically Black Protestant: Ask what Scripture says angels really are, and compare the Seele plan to Babel; then talk about why Shinji's choice to live with others is a choice for hope.
neon-genesis-evangelion.Atheist: The story's answer is human: people caused the disaster and people choose to repair it; talk about why Shinji picks painful life with others over painless merger.
neon-genesis-evangelion.Agnostic: Talk about the symbols the story borrows without explaining, and why it leaves some mysteries open; ask whether the adults' reasons for sending kids to fight ever hold up.
neon-genesis-evangelion.Nothing in particular: Gendo remembers loving his son only at the end; talk about late regret, family, and why Shinji's choice to keep living matters.

nisekoi.Historically Black Protestant: Raku and Chitoge lied to their fathers for years to keep the peace: was it right, and what did it cost? What does a good marriage need that the fake couple had to learn?
nisekoi.Atheist: Should a childhood promise bind an adult? How is a funny gang in a story different from real organized crime?
nisekoi.Agnostic: Is love something you are destined for or something you build? Kosaki loses gracefully; what makes that admirable?
nisekoi.Nothing in particular: Where is the line between parents guiding a child and controlling her, as with Marika's mother? Would Chitoge's hitting still be funny if the roles were reversed?

noragami.Historically Black Protestant: Yukine's wrongs make Yato sick until he confesses; how does that compare with what Scripture says about confession and cleansing (1 John 1:9)? How does a god who needs people's memory to exist compare with the God of the Bible?
noragami.Atheist: Yato was made to destroy; can someone become good if they were raised to do harm? Was Heaven's execution of Ebisu justice?
noragami.Agnostic: Gods in this story exist only while people remember them; what does it mean to be remembered? How do you think about humor and sacred things?
noragami.Nothing in particular: How do our choices affect the people tied to us? What keeps Hiyori and Yato connected even after she forgets him?

one-piece.Historically Black Protestant: The Celestial Dragons buy and sell people, and the heroes risk everything to free them; read it alongside Exodus and talk about why God hears the cry of the oppressed. Ask why Fisher Tiger's and Hody's anger is understood but revenge is still rejected (Romans 12:19).
one-piece.Atheist: The people who claim to be gods turn out to be tyrants. Ask why the government at Ohara wanted history erased, and why knowing the truth matters so much to Robin.
one-piece.Agnostic: The Void Century is a mystery the story keeps open for over a thousand chapters. Ask what the powerful gain by controlling what people are allowed to know.
one-piece.Nothing in particular: Luffy never leaves a friend behind and never rules the islands he frees. Ask what makes someone a real friend, and what makes a leader worth following.

one-punch-man.Historically Black Protestant: Saitama saves the city and lets others take the credit; read Matthew 6:1-4 together and talk about doing good when no one notices. Ask whether Mumen Rider was brave or foolish to fight a battle he knew he would lose.
one-punch-man.Atheist: Saitama's power comes from an ordinary routine, not magic or destiny. Ask why winning everything did not make him happy, and what the hero rankings say about chasing popularity.
one-punch-man.Agnostic: The story never tells us what will cure Saitama's boredom. Ask your child where they think meaning comes from when you already have what you wanted.
one-punch-man.Nothing in particular: The weakest hero gets the most respect. Talk about giving up credit for others, and how rankings and likes can make people care more about image than about helping.

orange.Historically Black Protestant: Talk about Galatians 6:2 and how the friends carry Kakeru; then ask who else he could have turned to, including a pastor, a counselor or a trusted adult.
orange.Atheist: Kakeru's worth does not depend on anything he does; talk about warning signs in a friend and why telling an adult matters even when a friend asks you not to.
orange.Agnostic: The future selves cannot fix their own world, only help another; ask whether it is still worth trying, and what regrets you could act on now.
orange.Nothing in particular: Ask how Kakeru seemed fine on the outside, what the friends noticed, and who you would tell if a friend seemed to be in danger.

oshi-no-ko.Historically Black Protestant: John 15:13 speaks of laying down one's life; is that the same as what Aqua does? Proverbs 18:21 says death and life are in the power of the tongue: how do the comments in vol. 3 show that?
oshi-no-ko.Atheist: How was Akane's image edited to make her a villain? What evidence should we want before joining a pile-on?
oshi-no-ko.Agnostic: The story never explains why Aqua and Ruby were reborn; does it need to? Can a lie told for love become true?
oshi-no-ko.Nothing in particular: Aqua gave his whole second life to revenge; what did it cost him and the people who loved him? What would you do if a friend were being mobbed online?

our-dreams-at-dusk.Historically Black Protestant: Talk about how the drop-in center welcomes an outcast and what the church is called to be for a hurting teen; then about where this story's view of marriage and gender differs from your church's teaching.
our-dreams-at-dusk.Atheist: Ask what made Tasuku's life worth living when he felt alone, and what makes an apology like Tsubaki's real.
our-dreams-at-dusk.Agnostic: Someone-san never tells anyone who they are; talk about whether that is kinder or less helpful than giving advice.
our-dreams-at-dusk.Nothing in particular: Saki is outed by someone who meant no harm; talk about whose story it is to tell, and about being a safe person for a friend.

pandora-hearts.Historically Black Protestant: Oz is told his existence is a sin: what does Scripture say about a person's worth before God? Isla Yura sells a false paradise for money; how do we tell a true shepherd from a false one?
pandora-hearts.Atheist: Why do Oz and Alice choose a hard truth over a perfect dream? How does the cult keep people believing something its leader knows is false?
pandora-hearts.Agnostic: If your memories and even your body were not your own, what would make you you? The ending imagines rebirth; what do you think happens after death?
pandora-hearts.Nothing in particular: Gilbert keeps his promise for a hundred years: what promises matter most to you? Ada forgives Vincent without conditions; was that wise?

parasyte.Historically Black Protestant: Migi says humans are closer to demons because they eat so much; talk about what Scripture says about sin and about humans made in God's image, and why the story lands on mercy. Ask how your family views Shinichi and Satomi's choice in ch. 57.
parasyte.Atheist: The story says reason alone does not make us human, feeling and mercy do; ask whether you agree and what that means for how we treat others.
parasyte.Agnostic: Hirokawa and Uragami both call humans the real parasites; ask how their views are alike and how the story answers them.
parasyte.Nothing in particular: Shinichi spares Gotou and then kills him; ask which choice was right and why he cries.

please-go-home-miss-akutsu.Historically Black Protestant: Akutsu stays overnight with no adults around and the parents just smile; talk about why your family sets boundaries and how 1 Thessalonians 4:3-4 speaks to dating. Ask what the story gets right about loyalty and care.
please-go-home-miss-akutsu.Atheist: Ask whether Akutsu's teasing about his adult videos and her body would read differently if the roles were reversed, and what respecting boundaries looks like.
please-go-home-miss-akutsu.Agnostic: Oyama only confesses when he thinks she is asleep; ask why honesty is so hard for both of them.
please-go-home-miss-akutsu.Nothing in particular: Akutsu's parents met the same way; ask whether that makes the arrangement wise or just lucky, and whether Oyama should skip college to stay near her.

pluto.Historically Black Protestant: The KR group hunts robots the way the Klan hunted people; how does the story show hatred of a group as sin? Atom chooses not to take revenge; compare Matthew 5:44.
pluto.Atheist: Gesicht and Atom are machines, yet we grieve them; what makes someone a person?
pluto.Agnostic: Can a made mind have a soul? Does the story answer, or leave it to you?
pluto.Nothing in particular: Hatred passes from one character to the next; who finally stops it, and how?

prison-school.Historically Black Protestant: Read Matthew 5:28 next to the peeping that starts the story, and ask what loyalty like Gakuto's looks like without the degrading jokes; this one is for adults.
prison-school.Atheist: Ask who is being laughed at and why, and whether a joke built on humiliating someone's body respects their dignity.
prison-school.Agnostic: Both councils abuse their power; talk about what the story says about people who hold power over others, and when a joke stops being funny.
prison-school.Nothing in particular: Gakuto's loyalty is the good part; the publisher rates it 18+, so check whether it fits your reader at all.

real.Historically Black Protestant: Where does hope come from for Takahashi, and where does Scripture say it comes from (Romans 5:3-5)? Does Nomiya earn forgiveness or receive it?
real.Atheist: The story never promises a miracle; what actually helps these young men keep going?
real.Agnostic: Is Takahashi's crash a punishment, a test, or just something that happened? The story leaves room to ask.
real.Nothing in particular: Takahashi used to rank people from A to E. What changed his mind, and who helped?

record-of-ragnarok.Historically Black Protestant: The Bible's God delivers the oppressed (Exodus); how is that different from these gods, who want to destroy humanity? Why might it trouble a believer to see Jesus as a silent spectator at a death match?
record-of-ragnarok.Atheist: The humans win respect by fighting; can human worth be shown in other ways? Is it fair to use other people's sacred figures as fighters?
record-of-ragnarok.Agnostic: If the gods in the story are real but cruel, does that make them worthy of worship? How should a storyteller handle figures that millions of people hold sacred?
record-of-ragnarok.Nothing in particular: Adam fights for his children without hating anyone; what makes that admirable? Should a murderer like Jack the Ripper represent the human race?

relife.Historically Black Protestant: Kaizaki tried to defend Saiki and it made things worse: how do we stand up for someone with wisdom and their consent? Where does real hope come from when life falls apart?
relife.Atheist: Is erasing people's memories 'for their own good' ever right, even if they never know? Is quitting a harmful job a failure or a brave choice?
relife.Agnostic: Why does the story say diligence alone, without help, can be dangerous? What does it take to start over?
relife.Nothing in particular: Ohga hides his brother's struggles out of shame; why do families hide mental-health problems, and what helps? Who could you reach out to if you felt stuck like Kaizaki?

rent-a-girlfriend.Historically Black Protestant: Was lying to the grandmothers kind or wrong, and what does Ephesians 4:25 say about it? Kazuya's best moment is the film he makes for Sayuri; what does that show about real love?
rent-a-girlfriend.Atheist: What does the story suggest money can and cannot buy? Does Sayuri's idea of 'lies that protect a truth' convince you?
rent-a-girlfriend.Agnostic: Kazuya gave Chizuru years of help; did that mean she owed him a relationship? Why did ch. 380 divide readers?
rent-a-girlfriend.Nothing in particular: Is rental companionship honest work, a harmless fiction or a problem? How does the story treat Kazuya's lust: are we meant to laugh, judge or sympathize?

ruridragon.Historically Black Protestant: Ruri's classmates choose to make room for someone who could be feared; talk about how your church family welcomes people who are different, and ask whether the class's rules for her were fair.
ruridragon.Atheist: The story explains dragons with genes and blood tests; ask how the class balanced safety and fairness without anyone being cast out.
ruridragon.Agnostic: Maeda judged Ruri before knowing her; ask how she found out she was wrong, and how you change your mind about someone.
ruridragon.Nothing in particular: Ruri's mother calls her choice to raise Ruri alone selfish; ask what each of them meant and what makes a family.

sakamoto-days.Historically Black Protestant: Sakamoto spares Uzuki and leaves him to the courts; how does that fit Romans 12:17-21? Can a man who has taken lives truly start over, and what does 2 Corinthians 5:17 say?
sakamoto-days.Atheist: Is non-lethal violence a different moral thing, or a smaller version of the same thing? Should a story's message apply to all its heroes, like Nagumo?
sakamoto-days.Agnostic: Uzuki was abused and tricked into killing someone he loved; how responsible is he?
sakamoto-days.Nothing in particular: Why might a rule kept every day change a person more than one big decision? When is a joke about someone's body funny, and when does it hurt?

seraph-of-the-end.Historically Black Protestant: The children in Sanguinem are kept in bondage, and Yu wants them free. Compare that hope with the Exodus, and ask whether a power that comes from a demon can ever be trusted (1 John 4:1).
seraph-of-the-end.Atheist: Yu will not trade Mika's life for the world. Ask whether a promise to one person can outweigh many lives, and why the story calls raising the dead a crime.
seraph-of-the-end.Agnostic: The manga invents its own angels, God and apocalypse. Ask how a story can borrow sacred words while changing their meaning.
seraph-of-the-end.Nothing in particular: Guren could not let his friends stay dead, and that ended the world. Ask what it means to grieve well and to let loved ones rest.

shikimoris-not-just-a-cutie.Historically Black Protestant: Shikimori protects Izumi and he cooks for her. Talk about strength and gentleness in men and women, and what your family believes should come before sharing a home.
shikimoris-not-just-a-cutie.Atheist: Ask what makes their relationship healthy, and how they handle a problem (his bad luck) that can never be fixed.
shikimoris-not-just-a-cutie.Agnostic: Ask whether luck is real, and how people live well with what they cannot control.
shikimoris-not-just-a-cutie.Nothing in particular: Ask how Shikimori treats Kamiya, who likes Izumi too, and what you would have done.

skip-and-loafer.Historically Black Protestant: Mitsumi studies hard so she can serve the town that raised her; talk about education as service. Ask how Mitsumi treats Nao when strangers mock her on the train, and how your family speaks of people whose lives differ from your teaching.
skip-and-loafer.Atheist: Shima thinks his kindness is fake; ask what makes kindness real and why he learned to perform it.
skip-and-loafer.Agnostic: Chieri says Mitsumi has never gone without affection; ask how a loving home shapes the way people treat others.
skip-and-loafer.Nothing in particular: Shima's mother hurt him and later apologized; ask what she owes him and what, if anything, he owes her.

slam-dunk.Historically Black Protestant: Mitsui comes back in tears and Coach Anzai takes him in before he proves anything. Compare that with the prodigal son, and talk about why a nickname like 'Gorilla' can wound.
slam-dunk.Atheist: What actually made Sakuragi good: talent, or 20,000 practice shots? How did his teammates help him change?
slam-dunk.Agnostic: Anzai was once the harsh 'White-Haired Devil.' What changed him, and can adults change too?
slam-dunk.Nothing in particular: Sakuragi keeps playing with a hurt back. Was that brave or a mistake, and what would you do for your team?

smoking-behind-the-supermarket.Historically Black Protestant: Sasaki finds rest in a smoke break. Read Matthew 11:28 and 1 Corinthians 6:19-20: where does lasting rest come from, and how should we care for our bodies?
smoking-behind-the-supermarket.Atheist: After the X-ray scare, Sasaki goes back to smoking. What does the evidence say, and is the story honest about it?
smoking-behind-the-supermarket.Agnostic: Yamada hides who she is so she can speak freely. Is that a lie, a kindness, or both?
smoking-behind-the-supermarket.Nothing in particular: Years ago Sasaki stood up for a stranger and never knew it mattered. Why might the story make that the root of everything?

so-im-a-spider-so-what.Historically Black Protestant: Kumoko is proud and self-reliant; compare Proverbs 16:18. Is her pride a strength, a danger, or both?
so-im-a-spider-so-what.Atheist: Kumoko figures out her world by testing it; how is that like science?
so-im-a-spider-so-what.Agnostic: The gods here run the world like a game; what would make a god worth trusting?
so-im-a-spider-so-what.Nothing in particular: Kumoko never asks for help; when should we?

solanin.Historically Black Protestant: How do Meiko's friends help her grieve, and what does a church family add when someone dies? Is Taneda's return to a regular job giving up or growing up?
solanin.Atheist: What does it mean to carry on someone's work after they die? Meiko quits hoping for freedom; what does she find instead?
solanin.Agnostic: Meiko's mother says happiness need not be the hard road; do you agree? Why might the author leave the cause of Taneda's crash unclear?
solanin.Nothing in particular: What makes an ordinary life good when a big dream does not come true? Who would you lean on in a loss like Meiko's?

soul-eater.Historically Black Protestant: Maka beats fear with courage. Compare that with 1 John 4:18, 'perfect love casts out fear.' Why does the church warn against witchcraft, even when a story makes witches friendly?
soul-eater.Atheist: Death cut away his fear to make a perfect order, and his fear became a monster. What happens when people try to get rid of fear completely?
soul-eater.Agnostic: Justin says, 'We choose the god who suits us.' Is that true of people? What is the difference between searching honestly and choosing what is convenient?
soul-eater.Nothing in particular: Crona was abused by their mother and later did terrible things. How much is Crona responsible, and what does Maka's patience with Crona teach?

spy-x-family.Historically Black Protestant: The Forgers take in a child no one else wanted; talk about adoption into God's family (Romans 8:15) and caring for orphans. Ask whether it is ever right to lie to people you love, and what the Bible says about truth in a home.
spy-x-family.Atheist: Nothing supernatural fixes anything here; people do, by caring and thinking. Ask why Henry was arrested for calling a speech propaganda, and when it is worth speaking out.
spy-x-family.Agnostic: The series has not yet said what happens when the lies come out. Ask your child what they think will happen, and whether a family built on a cover story can still be real.
spy-x-family.Nothing in particular: Ask what makes a family real: blood, papers, or what people do for each other. Talk about Yor's job and whether the comedy makes violence seem too easy.

sun-ken-rock.Historically Black Protestant: Ken protects the weak but builds his power on gambling and sex businesses. Talk about whether good ends can make a bad trade right, and about the dignity of an abused person.
sun-ken-rock.Atheist: Ken says no one can defile another person's body. Ask whether that answers the critics who say the story uses assault as decoration.
sun-ken-rock.Agnostic: The author changed his ending after a victim's family rejected hatred. Ask whether forgiving is harder than fighting.
sun-ken-rock.Nothing in particular: Tae-Soo says gangs and countries are the same thing. Ask where he is right and where he is wrong.

takopis-original-sin.Historically Black Protestant: The title borrows the phrase 'original sin'; how do the adults' wrongs pass down to the children? Naoki finds peace only after he confesses; compare 1 John 1:9.
takopis-original-sin.Atheist: Every gadget Takopi uses makes things worse; what actually helped Naoki and Shizuka?
takopis-original-sin.Agnostic: The story names no single villain; is it fair to blame the bully, the parents, or no one?
takopis-original-sin.Nothing in particular: If a friend seemed as alone as Shizuka, what would you do, and which adult would you tell?

teasing-master-takagi-san.Historically Black Protestant: 1 Corinthians 13:4 says love is patient and kind; where do you see that in Takagi and Nishikata? Is teasing ever unkind, and how can you tell?
teasing-master-takagi-san.Atheist: Nothing dramatic happens, yet the story feels meaningful; what makes small days matter?
teasing-master-takagi-san.Agnostic: Takagi always seems to know what Nishikata feels; how do we learn to read other people?
teasing-master-takagi-san.Nothing in particular: Nishikata keeps trying and never wins; is that a good thing? What makes teasing friendly rather than mean?

that-time-i-got-reincarnated-as-a-slime.Historically Black Protestant: When Tempest is attacked, Rimuru chooses vengeance; what does Romans 12:17-21 ask of us when we are wronged? Why might the story make a Demon Lord and his demons the heroes?
that-time-i-got-reincarnated-as-a-slime.Atheist: Rimuru needed about 10,000 souls but killed about 20,000 soldiers; does the number matter? What should limit a ruler's power?
that-time-i-got-reincarnated-as-a-slime.Agnostic: Is a kind ruler with unlimited power a good thing? What protects people if the ruler changes?
that-time-i-got-reincarnated-as-a-slime.Nothing in particular: Was Rimuru's rule against fighting humans wise? Naming gives monsters dignity but binds them to Rimuru; is that friendship, leadership or ownership?

the-100-girlfriends.Historically Black Protestant: Rentaro is honest and kind, but ask what Genesis 2:24 says about one man and one woman, and whether the jokes about adults and students would pass the Philippians 4:8 test.
the-100-girlfriends.Atheist: The story is good at showing honesty and fairness among friends; ask why its care about consent stops at the vice principal's gag and the adult staff.
the-100-girlfriends.Agnostic: Talk about what makes the group work in the story (honesty, no competition) and whether the same rules would work in real life, and where the story's jokes cross a line.
the-100-girlfriends.Nothing in particular: The chosen-family message is warm, but this one is rated for mature readers: check the age of the reader and talk about adults who date students.

the-apothecary-diaries.Historically Black Protestant: Maomao is sold into a palace and keeps her integrity there. Compare her with Esther (Esther 4:14): what helps each woman stay herself?
the-apothecary-diaries.Atheist: How does Maomao test a claim before she believes it? Try her method on a rumor you have heard.
the-apothecary-diaries.Agnostic: Many 'curses' turn out to have natural causes. Do you think every mystery will?
the-apothecary-diaries.Nothing in particular: Maomao helps people without wanting credit. Why might that matter to her?

the-case-study-of-vanitas.Historically Black Protestant: Ask whether the story's 'Church' matches the church your family knows, and talk about why no one is beyond God's love; then about the forced kiss and what real love looks like.
the-case-study-of-vanitas.Atheist: Moreau is a warning about science without ethics; talk about why some things should never be done to a person no matter the result.
the-case-study-of-vanitas.Agnostic: Every side in the story has both villains and good people; ask what that says about judging whole groups.
the-case-study-of-vanitas.Nothing in particular: Talk about how Noé and Vanitas stay friends after a terrible fight, and why the story treats drinking someone's blood without asking as a crime.

the-climber.Historically Black Protestant: Mori tries to live entirely alone. Compare that with the church as family and with Hebrews 12:1 on running with endurance. Where does Mori's hope come from, and where would yours?
the-climber.Atheist: If this life is all there is, why does surviving matter more than the summit in the end?
the-climber.Agnostic: Why do you think the manga lets Mori survive when the real climber died? What does that choice say?
the-climber.Nothing in particular: Danger made Mori feel alive. What are safer ways to feel that way, and what did Hana and the child give him that the mountain could not?

the-dangers-in-my-heart.Historically Black Protestant: Talk about 1 John 4:19 and how Anna's kindness changes Kyotaro; then about Ephesians 4:29 and the way the boys talk, and when your family thinks someone is ready to date.
the-dangers-in-my-heart.Atheist: Ask why Kyotaro imagined hurting his classmates at first and what he was protecting himself from.
the-dangers-in-my-heart.Agnostic: Has someone ever seen something good in you before you saw it yourself? Talk about what Anna saw in Kyotaro.
the-dangers-in-my-heart.Nothing in particular: Talk about how the boys in the class talk about girls, whether the story agrees with them, and whether 14 is too young to date.

the-eminence-in-shadow.Historically Black Protestant: Cid pretends to be ordinary but lives for glory. Read Matthew 6:1-4: what is the difference between real humility and a costume of humility?
the-eminence-in-shadow.Atheist: Cid's followers believe everything he says. How would you test a leader's claims instead of just trusting him?
the-eminence-in-shadow.Agnostic: Cid made up a story and it turned out to be true. Is he responsible for what people did because of it?
the-eminence-in-shadow.Nothing in particular: Cid enjoys fighting bandits because they are 'bad people.' Does that make it okay?

the-fable.Historically Black Protestant: Akira repays every kindness done to him; who in your life has shown you that kind of care? Romans 12:19 leaves vengeance to God; how does that sit beside the gangsters' justice here?
the-fable.Atheist: The Boss's order works because Akira chooses to keep it; is choosing not to kill the same as becoming a good person?
the-fable.Agnostic: Akira was raised to kill and learns another life; how much can a person change what they were made into?
the-fable.Nothing in particular: Kuroshio wants to be like Akira; why do the older men keep telling him no?

the-flowers-of-evil.Historically Black Protestant: Kasuga's secret theft grows until it is found out. Compare that with 1 John 1:9 on confession. Nakamura wants 'the other side'; what hope does she lack, and who could she have talked to?
the-flowers-of-evil.Atheist: Nakamura says everyone is a hypocrite underneath. Is she right about anything? What does Kasuga find that makes life livable without her escape?
the-flowers-of-evil.Agnostic: The story never argues Nakamura out of her view; it just steps away from her ending. Is that a fair way to answer despair?
the-flowers-of-evil.Nothing in particular: Who was hurt by Kasuga's theft, including the girls who never appear? If a friend talked about wanting to 'go to the other side,' who could they talk to?

the-fragrant-flower-blooms-with-dignity.Historically Black Protestant: The two schools judge each other by uniform and neighborhood. How does the church teach us to see people God's way, and where have you seen a dividing wall come down?
the-fragrant-flower-blooms-with-dignity.Atheist: What actually changed each side's mind about the other school? Is there a stereotype you held that changed when you met someone?
the-fragrant-flower-blooms-with-dignity.Agnostic: Ms. Toki's rule came from guilt and a wish to protect. Can someone be wrong and still have good reasons?
the-fragrant-flower-blooms-with-dignity.Nothing in particular: Rintaro does not fight back when he is insulted. Is that strength or weakness, and how would you handle it?

the-girl-from-the-other-side.Historically Black Protestant: The story's church burns people out of fear. Read 1 John 4:18: how is Teacher's love different from the fear that drives the Inside?
the-girl-from-the-other-side.Atheist: Teacher is kind with nothing to gain. Where does kindness come from if not from reward or command?
the-girl-from-the-other-side.Agnostic: The story never explains the curse or the gods. Why might the author leave those questions open?
the-girl-from-the-other-side.Nothing in particular: Auntie left Shiva in the forest to save her. Was that love, abandonment, or both?

the-guy-she-was-interested-in-wasnt-a-gu.Historically Black Protestant: Joe gave up his own plans to raise Mitsuki: what does the story say about sacrifice for family? Your church has its own teaching about love and marriage; where does this story agree with it, and where does it not?
the-guy-she-was-interested-in-wasnt-a-gu.Atheist: What do you hide to fit in, and what would happen if you stopped? Was Mitsuki's disguise a lie, a defense, or both?
the-guy-she-was-interested-in-wasnt-a-gu.Agnostic: Why is Aya hurt by the deception rather than by who Mitsuki turns out to be? What is worth compromising for a career?
the-guy-she-was-interested-in-wasnt-a-gu.Nothing in particular: How does sharing music help Aya and Mitsuki find each other? When Mitsuki is mocked, what does Aya do, and what would you do?

the-promised-neverland.Historically Black Protestant: Grace Field's children are raised as livestock and fight their way to freedom; read the Exodus story alongside it and talk about God hearing the cry of the oppressed. Ask how 'Him', who always takes a price, is different from a God whose grace is a gift (Ephesians 2:8).
the-promised-neverland.Atheist: The kids escape by thinking, testing and planning together. Ask whether Norman was wrong to want to destroy the demons after what they did, and why Emma refused.
the-promised-neverland.Agnostic: Ray, Norman and Emma each have a different answer to who you should save. Ask which one your child agrees with, and whether that changed by the end.
the-promised-neverland.Nothing in particular: Emma will not leave even the youngest behind, and she pays for it with her memories. Talk about loyalty to family and whether Isabella's last act changes how we judge her.

the-quintessential-quintuplets.Historically Black Protestant: Futaro works and studies to lift his family out of debt. How does that connect with what the church teaches about education and diligence? Several characters kiss him without asking; how should we honor one another (Romans 12:10)?
the-quintessential-quintuplets.Atheist: Several characters kiss Futaro while he is asleep or without asking. How does the story treat that, and how would you?
the-quintessential-quintuplets.Agnostic: The author wanted every sister to 'settle things' rather than be discarded. Did the ending succeed for all five?
the-quintessential-quintuplets.Nothing in particular: Ichika pretended to be her sister to win Futaro and later apologized. Was the apology enough? What makes an apology real?

the-rising-of-the-shield-hero.Historically Black Protestant: Naofumi's vindication echoes Joseph, but he also buys a child; read Exodus 21:16 or Philemon together and ask whether a kind owner makes slavery acceptable, and what deliverance for Raphtalia would have looked like.
the-rising-of-the-shield-hero.Atheist: The villain church claims a god's authority to justify hatred; ask how the story separates a corrupt institution from belief, and whether the queen's justice is fair or just revenge.
the-rising-of-the-shield-hero.Agnostic: Ask how a community should treat an accusation when it cannot yet know the truth, and what that means for both the accused and the accuser.
the-rising-of-the-shield-hero.Nothing in particular: The former king chooses to keep the name Trash; ask what real repentance looks like, and whether humiliating someone in public is justice.

the-seven-deadly-sins.Historically Black Protestant: The heroes are called 'Sins' and the villains 'Commandments': why might an author flip those names, and what does Scripture teach about each? How should someone who loves another person treat their body?
the-seven-deadly-sins.Atheist: Can a story's 'god' be a villain, and what does it mean to stand against unjust authority? Should Hendrickson and Dreyfus be forgiven for what they did while possessed?
the-seven-deadly-sins.Agnostic: Both the Supreme Deity and the Demon King curse the lovers; who decides what is right when the powers above disagree? Does Merlin deserve forgiveness?
the-seven-deadly-sins.Nothing in particular: Each Sin carries a vice; which character overcomes theirs? Why is Meliodas's touching a problem even when it is played as a joke?

the-summer-hikaru-died.Historically Black Protestant: The village offered lives for wishes and called it worship. Talk about what Scripture says of such bargains and of testing the spirits (1 John 4:1), and about how the story treats Yoshiki's feelings.
the-summer-hikaru-died.Atheist: The penance rituals did nothing, and research uncovers the truth. Ask whether a perfect copy of a person, with all his memories, is still that person.
the-summer-hikaru-died.Agnostic: The story never says what the creature is or where Hikaru's soul went. Ask whether some questions should stay open.
the-summer-hikaru-died.Nothing in particular: Yoshiki stays with something that frightens him because it is lonely. Ask when loyalty becomes control, and who in a town gets treated as a monster.

the-way-of-the-househusband.Historically Black Protestant: Tatsu becomes a new man; what does Scripture say makes a change last? How does this marriage, where she earns and he keeps house, compare with what your church teaches about family?
the-way-of-the-househusband.Atheist: Tatsu changed because he wanted a different life; what helps people leave violent groups in real life?
the-way-of-the-househusband.Agnostic: Why does everyone assume the worst about Tatsu? Have you ever been judged by how you look?
the-way-of-the-househusband.Nothing in particular: What makes Tatsu a good husband and neighbor? Is housework treated as real work in your home?

three-days-of-happiness.Historically Black Protestant: The shop says Kusunoki is worth 300,000 yen; Scripture says every person bears God's image. Where could Kusunoki have found hope and people to lean on before he despaired?
three-days-of-happiness.Atheist: If this life is the only one, what makes three happy days worth more or less than thirty empty years? Who could a friend talk to if they felt their life was worthless?
three-days-of-happiness.Agnostic: The story never explains the shop or says whether the ending was right. What do you think, and why might reasonable people disagree?
three-days-of-happiness.Nothing in particular: Kusunoki's life became worth more as he became kinder. Is that how life works? What would you say to a friend who thought their life did not matter?

to-your-eternity.Historically Black Protestant: The Beholder says pain promotes growth; what does Scripture say about suffering and hope? Bon and Kahaku both give their lives; how are their choices different?
to-your-eternity.Atheist: What does it mean to carry someone with you after they die? Why does Fushi refuse the power to control everything?
to-your-eternity.Agnostic: What kind of creator watches without feeling, and what changes when he becomes human? Why does the story end where it began?
to-your-eternity.Nothing in particular: Hayase says she loves Fushi; how can you tell love from possession? Why does Fushi let his friends go at the end?

toilet-bound-hanako-kun.Historically Black Protestant: Hanako killed his brother and hopes doing his duty will erase it. How is that different from forgiveness by grace? And why does the church warn against summoning spirits, even in fun?
toilet-bound-hanako-kun.Atheist: Every wish in this story costs someone else. Have you ever wanted something that would cost another person, and how did you decide?
toilet-bound-hanako-kun.Agnostic: Teru says spirits must be exorcised; Kou says they can be helped. Who is right, and how could anyone know?
toilet-bound-hanako-kun.Nothing in particular: Nene says she never wished for Aoi to die in her place. Is she responsible anyway? What should a friend do when someone says they want to disappear?

tokyo-ghoul-re.Historically Black Protestant: Kaneki says he will try to bear his sins (ch. 159); compare Isaiah 53:4-6 and 1 John 1:9. When a law like Article 88 punishes anyone who shelters the hunted, what does conscience require (Acts 5:29)?
tokyo-ghoul-re.Atheist: Furuta decides that because everything ends, nothing matters; how would you answer him? What does the CCG being run by ghouls say about institutions built on fear?
tokyo-ghoul-re.Agnostic: The story borrows the language of sin and the Lord without a God who acts; what does that borrowed language add?
tokyo-ghoul-re.Nothing in particular: Arima chooses to die so Kaneki can carry on: how do you see his choice? Does Mutsuki's forgiveness feel earned?

tokyo-ghoul.Historically Black Protestant: The CCG treats ghouls as vermin; how does the story show what hatred of a whole group does? Romans 12:21 says overcome evil with good; does anyone here manage it?
tokyo-ghoul.Atheist: Is being human about biology or about how we treat others?
tokyo-ghoul.Agnostic: Kaneki belongs to two worlds and fits in neither; how do we live with questions about who we are?
tokyo-ghoul.Nothing in particular: Hide stays a friend no matter what; what does that kind of loyalty look like in real life?

tokyo-revengers.Historically Black Protestant: Takemichi never gives up on Mikey; compare it with the shepherd who goes after the one lost sheep (Luke 15:4). Talk honestly about gangs: the story shows they end in death or prison even though the jackets look cool, and ask what a real family and church family give that a gang cannot.
tokyo-revengers.Atheist: No one in the story gets help from above; Takemichi just keeps showing up. Ask why the strongest fighter, Mikey, is the one who most needs saving.
tokyo-revengers.Agnostic: Every time Takemichi fixes one thing, something else goes wrong. Ask what the story is saying about cause and effect, and whether you can ever fully undo a mistake.
tokyo-revengers.Nothing in particular: Ask what the gang gives these boys that they don't get at home, and what it costs them. Talk about Baji's choice and whether there was a better way to stop a cycle of revenge.

tomie.Historically Black Protestant: Every man who tries to own Tomie is destroyed. Talk about how desire gives birth to sin (James 1:14-15) and what the adults in story 1 owed a 15-year-old.
tomie.Atheist: Ask what turns ordinary people into killers in these stories, and whether the critics who say the stories blame the woman are right.
tomie.Agnostic: Ito never explains what Tomie is. Ask whether a story can teach something good when it has no good characters.
tomie.Nothing in particular: Tsukiko and Fumihito are not pulled in. Ask what helps a person resist something everyone around them gives in to.

tomo-chan-is-a-girl.Historically Black Protestant: Jun asks Tomo's father before they date. What does honoring parents (Ephesians 6:1-3) look like in a friendship that becomes a romance?
tomo-chan-is-a-girl.Atheist: Jun stayed silent for years to protect the friendship. When is silence kind, and when does it hurt?
tomo-chan-is-a-girl.Agnostic: Misuzu thought Tomo had to change to be loved. Who decides what a girl 'should' be?
tomo-chan-is-a-girl.Nothing in particular: After Tomo is groped, Jun tells her to stop wearing skirts. What is wrong with that advice, and who is responsible for an assault?

tomodachi-game.Historically Black Protestant: Yuichi saves his friends by lying and blackmailing. Talk about whether good ends justify deceit (Proverbs 12:22) and what real repentance would require of him.
tomodachi-game.Atheist: The game rewards anyone who doubts a friend. Ask whether trust can be rational, and whether Yuichi deserves the forgiveness the author hoped for.
tomodachi-game.Agnostic: Ask whether it is ever right to lie to a friend to protect them, as Tenji and Yuichi both do.
tomodachi-game.Nothing in particular: Yuichi says friends matter more than money. Ask whether he treats people who are not his friends as if they matter.

usogui.Historically Black Protestant: Baku wins by lying to liars; read Proverbs 12:22 and ask whether deceiving a deceiver is different. Talk about the arc where police frame scapegoats and why exposing that matters.
usogui.Atheist: Kakerou enforces every wager, fair or not; ask whether a rule-keeper who cares nothing for justice is good or evil.
usogui.Agnostic: Ask whether life is really a gamble everyone is already making, or whether that is just the gambler's way of seeing it.
usogui.Nothing in particular: Kaji's mother treated him like something to cash in; ask how he learns what he is worth, and whether the villains' executions are justice or revenge.

uzumaki.Historically Black Protestant: 2 Timothy 1:7 says God has not given us a spirit of fear; how does that sit beside a story built entirely on fear? At the end Kirie stops fighting and holds Shuichi: is that giving up, or love, and what does Lamentations 3:21-23 say about hope?
uzumaki.Atheist: Shuichi is right all along; why does being right not help him? Is the story about the limits of reason, or about fear itself?
uzumaki.Agnostic: Ito himself is not sure what the spiral means; does a mystery need an answer to be meaningful?
uzumaki.Nothing in particular: Mr. Saito loves spirals and his wife hates them, and both are destroyed; what is the story saying about obsession and fear? Can a story with no hope still be worth reading?

vagabond.Historically Black Protestant: Musashi learns most when he loses; compare his road from pride to humility with Proverbs 16:18 and James 4:6. Talk about where the story finds peace (Zen) and where your family finds it, and check the sexual content before handing it to a teen.
vagabond.Atheist: No god or magic helps Musashi; only practice, defeat and other people change him. Ask why the most famous battle leaves him broken instead of proud, and what strength is for.
vagabond.Agnostic: The series never reached its ending, so the final duel is never drawn. Ask your reader what they think Musashi was looking for, and whether he was getting closer.
vagabond.Nothing in particular: Ask why Matahachi, who does almost everything wrong, is the one forgiven and still alive to tell the story. Talk about finding your own path without needing to be the best.

vinland-saga.Historically Black Protestant: Thorfinn learns that the bravest thing is to refuse to hit back; compare ch. 96 with Matthew 5:38-44 and the nonviolent courage of the Civil Rights movement. Talk about Arnheid and Einar, and why freedom from slavery is at the center of Vinland.
vinland-saga.Atheist: No god steps in; Thorfinn has to face what he did and choose who to become. Ask whether he can ever make up for the people he killed, and who gets to decide that.
vinland-saga.Agnostic: Canute decides to build paradise on earth by force, even against God; Thorfinn tries to build it without force. Ask which plan your teen finds more realistic, and which more right.
vinland-saga.Nothing in particular: Ask what a true warrior is, and why Thors says he needs no sword. Talk about Hild, who has every reason for revenge, and what it takes to let it go.

we-never-learn.Historically Black Protestant: Nariyuki studies to lift his widowed mother and siblings; talk about education as a calling and a gift to family. Ask which scenes treat a girl's body as the joke and how that fits Philippians 4:8.
we-never-learn.Atheist: The fireworks legend turns out to be invented; ask why people want legends like that to be true, and whether effort really beats talent here.
we-never-learn.Agnostic: Mafuyu thought students should stick to what they are best at; ask whether she was wrong or partly right.
we-never-learn.Nothing in particular: Ask what being useful means in this story, and how a scene would feel different if the girl being joked about were your friend.

welcome-to-demon-school-iruma-kun.Historically Black Protestant: Iruma is rescued from parents who sold him; talk about Psalm 27:10, and about where your family draws the line on friendly demon characters and calling evil good, even as a joke.
welcome-to-demon-school-iruma-kun.Atheist: Ask why Iruma and Kiriwo turn out so differently when both had families that failed them, and what that says about where kindness comes from.
welcome-to-demon-school-iruma-kun.Agnostic: Talk about why learning to say no, and to want things for yourself, is part of growing up.
welcome-to-demon-school-iruma-kun.Nothing in particular: Sullivan loves Iruma before he has done anything to earn it; talk about who plays that role in your life.

witch-hat-atelier.Historically Black Protestant: The word witch here means a trained craftsperson; talk about what Scripture forbids and whether this story crosses that line for your family. Who in the story is shut out of learning, and how does that compare with the church's fight for education?
witch-hat-atelier.Atheist: Magic in this world is a skill anyone can learn by careful study. Should dangerous knowledge ever be kept secret for safety, and who should decide?
witch-hat-atelier.Agnostic: The law and the rebels both have good reasons and bad methods. Which side do you think has the stronger case so far, and what would change your mind?
witch-hat-atelier.Nothing in particular: Coco made a terrible mistake by accident and spends the story trying to make it right. What do we owe the people we hurt, even by accident?

wotakoi.Historically Black Protestant: Many of the friends' honest talks happen over drinks; what does your church teach about alcohol, and where else can adults open up to each other? Hanako and Kabakura insult each other but stay together; what does Ephesians 4:29 say about how we speak to those we love?
wotakoi.Atheist: Narumi hides her hobbies at work for fear of judgment; when is privacy wise and when is hiding a burden? What makes a hobby healthy?
wotakoi.Agnostic: Hirotaka lets Narumi open up at her own pace; why does that matter in a relationship?
wotakoi.Nothing in particular: Kou thinks of herself as a burden; how did Naoya help her? What does a lasting relationship need besides shared hobbies?

yamada-kun-and-the-seven-witches.Historically Black Protestant: Yamada wishes the powers away for everyone instead of himself; talk about Philippians 2:4. Ask who should decide whether a kiss happens, and how the bath-scene jokes fit Philippians 4:8.
yamada-kun-and-the-seven-witches.Atheist: The club figures out the witches by testing rules; ask how they would know if a power was real, and what the story says about consent when kisses are tools.
yamada-kun-and-the-seven-witches.Agnostic: Why is being forgotten the worst fate in this story? Ask what makes a person who they are if no one remembers them.
yamada-kun-and-the-seven-witches.Nothing in particular: The story calls peeping toms wrong but jokes about its heroes looking; ask whether that is fair.

yamada-kun-lv999.Historically Black Protestant: Yamada shows love by showing up; talk about 1 John 3:18 and about what Scripture says on waiting for marriage (1 Corinthians 6:18) next to ch. 69.
yamada-kun-lv999.Atheist: Trust here is earned by conduct over time; talk about safe rules for meeting people from online games, which the story itself raises.
yamada-kun-lv999.Agnostic: Ask whether the age gap matters and what would change your answer, and whether Akane's fake-boyfriend lie in ch. 1 was harmless.
yamada-kun-lv999.Nothing in particular: The guild is a good picture of friends who have your back; talk about drinking to forget, and about the age gap between Akane and Yamada.

yokohama-kaidashi-kikou.Historically Black Protestant: Read Ecclesiastes 3 beside Alpha's calm in a fading world, then ask what hope the story lacks that the resurrection gives.
yokohama-kaidashi-kikou.Atheist: Ask whether a life can be good without a future for the species, and what Alpha finds worth doing in the twilight.
yokohama-kaidashi-kikou.Agnostic: The author leaves many mysteries unexplained on purpose; talk about why some questions might be better left open.
yokohama-kaidashi-kikou.Nothing in particular: Talk about slowing down to notice small things, and about how the characters remember Ojisan and Sensei after they are gone.

yona-of-the-dawn.Historically Black Protestant: Yona decides not to take revenge on Su-won: is that weakness or strength, and what does Scripture say about leaving vengeance to God? Yona kills a man who traffics girls; when, if ever, is it right to take a life to protect others?
yona-of-the-dawn.Atheist: What makes a ruler legitimate: blood, power or service? Can a good person be a bad ruler, as King Il was?
yona-of-the-dawn.Agnostic: Does good rule ever make up for how someone got power? The dragons were born to serve; are they free?
yona-of-the-dawn.Nothing in particular: What turns a duty into a choice? How does Yona grow from a sheltered princess into someone people follow?

yotsuba.Historically Black Protestant: Koiwai only felt like a father when Yotsuba called him 'Daddy' (ch. 105); what does it mean that God adopts us as his children (Romans 8:15)? What helps you tell the truth when you have done something wrong?
yotsuba.Atheist: What does Yotsuba learn by testing things herself? What ordinary thing did you notice today that you usually ignore?
yotsuba.Agnostic: Yotsuba treats everything as a wonder; what in the world still makes you wonder?
yotsuba.Nothing in particular: What makes someone family? Why might something look cool, like Torako's smoking, but not be good for you?

zom-100.Historically Black Protestant: Akira escapes a job that treated him like a slave; compare Colossians 3:23 on working for the Lord rather than for people. Is doing what you want the same as living well?
zom-100.Atheist: The vaccine comes from science, not miracles; what does the story trust to save people?
zom-100.Agnostic: If you knew the world might end, what would be on your list, and why?
zom-100.Nothing in particular: Akira goes home to repay his parents; what do we owe the people who raised us?
